protocol.summary: I checked how faithfully scripts/prereg_conformance.py (SHA 0520ea58…, matches the procedure doc) and its configs and amendments follow PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex, the per-object registrations and CLARIFICATION_TIMING_RULE. The docstring matches the code except for small points. Most of the operationalisations are disclosed, and several are stricter than the written rules: 90% coverage, the per-event consistency check, beta >= 1, dips only, and INCONSISTENT needing SNR >= 7. However, two defects should block publication. (1) For TIC 70441745 the 130-min max() gate is far wider than T14/2 (45 min), and RECOVERED takes depth and SNR at the fitted offset, not at the predicted time. As a result, a dip that does not overlap the predicted transit at all is scored RECOVERED. I ran this on synthetic data and on real S106-free S96 noise: the conformance evaluator gave RECOVERED, while the frozen evaluator (which the timing addenda say governs) gave EXCLUDED on both. (2) For the two protocol objects, the product and reference values in the configs (QLP SAP_FLUX; 855 ppm and 1090 ppm / 2.84 h) depart from the protocol's explicit 'QLP DET_FLUX' and its 750 ppm / 2.0 h and 970 ppm / 2.9 h. This is not stated anywhere. The 120444365 amendment says the registration had no reference values, but leaves out that the protocol states them, even though the timing addendum in the same file says the protocol governs. I cannot tell which way this choice tilts without test data. The failure is a missing statement of which document governs, which REVIEW_timing_rule.md:369 had already asked for. Major issues: RECOVERED takes the best SNR over offsets and durations; on in-sample nulls this adds a median +1.76 SNR versus +0.37 on injections, and a proxy of the protocol's fixed-phase depth gives equal power. Validation and calibration were not run with the locked configs (T14 2.18 h vs 2.0 h; every run used sigma = 3 min, so gates of 48, 130 and 136 min were never tested). The duration rule accepts a range that depends on SNR, and its guard cases were only shown at SNR 46-105. INCONSISTENT is harder to reach (SNR >= 7, common offset only) than RECOVERED (SNR >= 5). The coverage rule redefines INSUFFICIENT. The promised per-event min() assessment was implemented as a joint fit. Four S106 registrations still point to the frozen evaluator. TIC 70441745 has no clock prior, so its test cannot be scored at all. The remaining issues are minor provenance and wording points. I used 12 conformance runs (1-4 s each) and 3 frozen-evaluator runs, all on synthetic or in-sample (sector <= 105) data. I opened no S106 photometry.
checks_done: All 7 SHA-256s in CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md:17-22 match the files on disk (shasum). The frozen scripts/prereg_test.py is still 630815cc…

Docstring vs code match: offset grid 2 min over ±432 min and duration grid 0.5-2.0x in 5% steps (l.153); median out-of-box baseline within ±3D minus in-box mean (l.102-105); MAD scatter x beta x sqrt(1/n_in+1/n_out) (l.105, l.61-68); VALID = depth>0, consistency p>=0.01, >=2 events positive at 1 sigma (l.164); band duration with delta-chi2<=4 (l.177); local window max(gate,30)+T14/2 (l.181); RECOVERED needs |o|<=gate (l.184); INCONSISTENT on the global band fit with SNR>=7 and |o|>max(gate,30) (l.187); EXCLUDED at offset 0 and reference duration (l.179,189); gate uses mean sigma over eligible events (l.156); mask ±(T14+max(3 sigma,30)) (l.131). Mismatches are listed as minor findings.

EXCLUDED at offset 0 and reference duration with >=2 fully covered events matches PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:53. The ±0.3 d search (offsets ±432 min) matches the INCONSISTENT window in PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:51.
wotan mask semantics: the flatten mask marks True points as excluded (site-packages/wotan/flatten.py:126-127,258). Both evaluators pass True for in-transit points, so the masking really happens.

Product clause: no SPOC 2-min S106 light curve exists for any of the 7 targets (0 matches for each zero-padded TIC in catalogs/bulk/tesscurl_sector_106_lc.sh, a URL list, not photometry). The protocol's 'SPOC PDCSAP if 2-min data exist' branch therefore does not apply, and only the DET_FLUX vs SAP_FLUX question is left.

Synthetic suite reproduced 15/15 from the conf_test/*.json outcome fields against the CASES expectations, all with version 'conformance-v2.0 (2026-10-20)'. conf_test outputs were written 2 s after the final code's mtime (22:28:46).

Calibration numbers in the procedure doc reproduced from conf_calib_*/summary.csv and conf_calib2_*/summary.csv: round 1 nulls 1 RECOVERED / 6 INCONSISTENT / 11 EXCLUDED of 49, injections 44/49; round 2 nulls 1 / 0 / 9 of 51, injections 46/51, min() 31/51.

The diff from results/qlp_clock_v2/prereg_conformance_v2.0_precalib.py to the final code is limited to the INCONSISTENT branch and its docstring. The pre-final conf_real runs (22:21) therefore have logically unchanged outcomes: RECOVERED is checked before INCONSISTENT, and the final INCONSISTENT rule is only stricter.

Locked 120444365 config (T14 2.0 h instead of the validation's 2.18 h) re-run on in-sample S105 and S96 transits: both still RECOVERED (wf_review/faithfulness/locked/*.json). S105 band fit +10 min, 2.3 h, SNR 6.29. S96 is noted under the validation finding.

Wide-gate null false-RECOVERED on real noise (70441745 S96, sigma 43.4, gate 130.2, ref 1829/1.5 h; 5 null phases): 0/5 RECOVERED, highest local band SNR 2.9 (wf_review/faithfulness/null70/null_*.json). The depth floor (0.5 x ref ≈ 4.8 sigma there) protects this object. Lower bound from the authors' 100 nulls: 3/100 at a 130-min gate vs 2/100 at 30 min.

Opposite ±35-min offsets (each event outside the 30-min gate): AMBIGUOUS at high SNR (wf_review/faithfulness/syn/opp35_hi.json) and in one low-SNR realisation (opp35_lo.json). The frozen evaluator's stacked-offset rule would score this RECOVERED, so conformance is stricter here. This is not a tilt.

strong_plus_weak at operating SNR: by the expected values, per-event depths of 1400 vs 100 ppm with per-event error ~235 ppm differ by ~3.9 sigma and fail p>=0.01. The consistency guard holds below the high-SNR regime used in the test.
Frozen evaluator default product for a QLP file is DET_FLUX (prereg_test.py:18). The S105 QLP file has both SAP_FLUX and DET_FLUX columns (header listing only).
TIC 206620592 S106 1x1 TESScut file in the scratchpad (s106/) is disclosed in ERRATUM_S106_DATA_AVAILABILITY_2026-10-20.md:35. I listed the filename only and did not open it.

Run accounting: 12 conformance-evaluator runs (in-process loading of the unmodified script by path, 1-4 s each) and 3 frozen-evaluator runs. All data were synthetic or in-sample (S96/S105). Nothing was written outside wf_review/faithfulness/ and no file in the NASA tree was modified.

code.summary:
I read all 200 lines of scripts/prereg_conformance.py, plus qlp_clock_test_sector.py, qlp_clock_v2.py, make_conformance_configs.py, all 7 S106 configs, the test and validation scripts, the protocol's outcome rules and the draft procedure document. The SHA-256 values in the procedure document match the files on disk. The arithmetic is mostly sound. NaN handling, the chi2 dof, coverage edge cases, the clock sign, the box/baseline windows and the regex all behave as intended.

The problems are in robustness and input validation, and several can silently mis-score a real test. Two are blockers:
- **Segment-edge ramps.** Ramps near segment edges are not handled, and errors use one global white-noise scatter. On the authors' own S105 validation light curve, one event 0.42 d after a 4.8% SAP ramp carries a -1572 ppm, -6.5 sigma artifact. That artifact produced the null EXCLUDED and pulled the 1x injection's RECOVERED fit to +26 min. A 0.5x-reference injection on the same light curve is EXCLUDED. The only false RECOVERED in calibration round 2 also involves two edge-adjacent events.
- **EXCLUDED is tested only at offset 0.** It has no timing tolerance, and its median baseline is pulled down by a displaced dip. With TIC 70441745 settings (gate 130 min, T14 90 min), a 0.3x-reference dip 100 min from the prediction (inside the registered gate) comes out EXCLUDED 76/100 times, against 0/100 when on time. Pure noise comes out EXCLUDED 56/100.

Major issues:
- EXCLUDED has no per-event consistency check, unlike RECOVERED.
- The red-noise beta is based on the MAD and floored at 1. It stays at exactly 1.0 on 183374279 S105, where the null z standard deviation is 5.1 (1.19 away from edges). On 120444365 the null z standard deviation is 1.3-1.5 at the reference duration and 1.8-2.0 at 2x.
- The clock record is never checked against the TIC, sector, light-curve file or predictions. A record for TIC 999 / S50 was applied and turned RECOVERED into EXCLUDED.
- A CSV light curve skips the sector/TIC header checks and the QUALITY filter.
- `--allow-no-clock` bypasses the declared clock gate without leaving any trace in the output.
- results/qlp_clock_v2/70441745.json is missing, so the clock script crashes and TIC 70441745 S106 cannot be scored as declared.

Minor issues are listed in the findings. Any fix changes the hash on line 17 of the procedure document, so it needs a VERSION bump to v2.1, a re-hash and a re-run of the synthetic suite before publication.

Run budget and one rule breach:
- **Runs:** 4 full subprocess evaluator runs and 4 in-process runs of the unchanged evaluator. The Monte Carlo used a further ~650 in-process runs, each about 0.5 s, with only the informational per-event free box fit replaced by a stub; that fit never feeds the outcome. The stubbed runs reproduce the authors' conf_real numbers exactly (e.g. 1x injection: RECOVERED, stack +271 +- 170, band fit at +26 min). Hard-rule check: no S106+ photometry was opened or downloaded, and scratchpad/s106 was not read.
- **Breach:** importing scripts/prereg_conformance.py in-process (without -B) may have written the bytecode cache scripts/__pycache__/prereg_conformance.cpython-312.pyc (timestamp 23:13). That is a generated file, not a change to project content. I did not delete it, because another agent may also have created it. The qlp_clock_v2 .pyc is dated 22:13, earlier than my session.

All fixtures are under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fernando-Desktop-NASA/c3c861f6-d690-49d9-96f5-051efe8a7e34/scratchpad/wf_review/code-correctness/.

Clock interpolation outside the event range: np.interp holds the end values (verified), and only times near events matter for scoring. PASS.
wotan in the venv is a modified build with a mask parameter: True means excluded from the fit and the trend is still evaluated there (flatten.py lines 126-130, 258). Mask semantics are correct. PASS.

Reproduced the authors' conf_real 183374279 S105 inject_halfphase result exactly in-process (RECOVERED, stack +271 +- 170, band fit +26 min / 2.27 h / 1406 ppm), which confirms the harness is faithful.

Evaluator runs: 4 full subprocess runs (R1 displaced 0.3x dip, R2 on-time 0.3x dip, R4 FITS without TICID, R6 real-data 0.5x injection near an edge) and 4 in-process unstubbed runs (R3a, R3b, R5a, R5b). Monte Carlo: about 650 in-process runs of the unchanged main() with only the informational fixed=None per-event box_fit stubbed out.

Hard rules: no Sector >= 106 photometry, cutouts or light curves were opened or downloaded; the clock-script probe for 70441745 was given a nonexistent --qlp path and crashed before any file access; scratchpad/s106 was not read. clock.summary:
The sign convention and the S105 numbers check out. The correction (LTT + c0 - (QLP - spacecraft)) is right, and prereg_conformance.py:128 adds it to the light-curve times. For TIC 183374279 S105 the tool gives +2.672 / +3.266 / +3.875 min. The middle value matches results/qlp_clock_v2/183374279.json (+3.266031) to 1e-10 min, but both use the same code, so this is a regression check rather than independent validation.

The clock procedure is not ready to publish. There are 2 blockers:
(1) The new CADENCENO check in the equal-length branch refuses every case. All 57 cached TESScut cutouts have CADENCENO = 0. Equal-length matching was used for 17/21 affected-sector and 36/36 control-sector clock measurements, and none of the authors' 198 validation clock records used this branch.
(2) In the unequal-length branch the measurement is taken from whichever file the data/qlp* glob finds first, not from the --qlp file whose hash is recorded.

There are 3 majors: the evaluator never checks that the clock record matches the TIC, sector or file; --allow-no-clock skips the clock gate without any flag; and the gap-edge method has no consistency check, so one misregistered gap changes corrections by up to 2.6 min. There are 6 minor items.

A record from a product MAST has already fixed comes out at about 0, but only in the gap-edge branch. No Sector 106 data were downloaded or opened. Nothing in the project, data/lk_cache or ~/.lightkurve changed during my runs. I made 3 evaluator runs and about 15 clock-tool runs (~2 s each). All temporary files are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fernando-Desktop-NASA/c3c861f6-d690-49d9-96f5-051efe8a7e34/scratchpad/wf_review/clock/.
checks_done: Sign convention, independent of the authors' code. Matching every S105 TESScut cadence (TIME - TIMECORR) to the nearest QLP time gives 11652/11652 at -3 s; S103 gives 10964/10964 at -3 s, so QLP S103/S105 TIME is spacecraft time with no barycentric term (indep.py).

LTT sign. The Horizons TESS-vector LTT (+2.588/+3.182/+3.791 min for S105, -3.334 for S103) agrees with an astropy Earth-centre calculation (no network) within 1 s. The TESScut TIMECORR at the same times has the same sign and is within 0.6 min (+3.27/+3.80/+4.33 and -3.45). So the correction LTT + c0 - off, added to QLP times, is right.

Evaluator adds the correction (prereg_conformance.py:127-128 t = t + corr). End to end on S105 FITS: epoch 243's best per-event offset is 0 / +3 / -3 min with clock corrections 0 / +2.67 / -3.25 min (runs E3 / E1 / E2).

Run A: qlp_clock_test_sector.py on S105 with a temporary config and a temporary prediction CSV (epochs 243 and 244 back-projected from final_ephemeris_v2.json, plus a row at 4220.78194670639). Anchor 'gap-edge (3 gaps)'; corrections 2.67169 / 3.26603 / 3.87483 min. The middle value equals results/qlp_clock_v2/183374279.json (3.266030590) to 1e-10 min; this is the same code path, so it is a regression check. It also matches the authors' conf_real record (2.6717 / 3.8748).

MAST-already-fixed case, gap-edge branch: a copy of the S105 QLP file with LTT + c0 - off added to TIME (s105_fixed, run with the file lookup patched to the copy) gives corrections +0.020 / -0.005 / +0.068 min, i.e. about 0. Nothing is assumed from the sector number. The equal-length branch refuses the correctly timed S96 control sector instead (Run B2).
The >= 2 gaps requirement works when the right file is measured: patched one-gap and no-gap copies are refused (exit 2). It is bypassed in the real tool (see blocker 2).
The 1-minute gap-length tolerance throws out a gap whose edge cadence is missing: dropping the first FFI after gap 2 leaves 'gap-edge (2 gaps)' with corrections unchanged to < 1e-5 min.

Whole-cadence shift (+200 s) of the whole file in gap-edge mode: measured as off = +3.2817 min and undone correctly; shifted time + correction = original + 2.6714 min against Run A's +2.6717. The equal-length branch refuses both the aligned copy and the +200 s copy with the same message, so it tells nothing apart.
Hashes of qlp_clock_test_sector.py (91f8abd2...) and qlp_clock_v2.py (e8c42beb...) match CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md lines 18-19; prereg_conformance.py is 0520ea58..., matching line 17.

TESScut download path: q.cut(tic, sec) calls lk.search_tesscut and downloads only when no cached cutout is found. In the tool it runs after the QLP SECTOR assert (qlp_clock_test_sector.py:20 before :22), so it needs a QLP file whose header says SECTOR 106. No other script calls it with sector 106: validate_conformance_real.py uses S105/S96 only, test_conformance.py uses product 'synthetic', make_conformance_configs.py never calls cut. At test time it will download a 3x3 S106 cube into data/lk_cache/clockcheck/<tic>/, which is expected.

Confirmed I triggered no Sector 106 access: all my configs used sectors 96/103/105, whose cutouts are cached. find -newer marker shows no new or changed files under /Users/fernando/Desktop/NASA (excluding .venv), data/lk_cache, ~/.lightkurve or ~/.astropy. There are no tess-s0106-* or tess-s0107-* cutouts under data/. scripts/__pycache__/qlp_clock_v2.cpython-312.pyc is dated 22:13, before my marker (23:13). I opened no Sector 106 or later file.

Seen but not opened: scratchpad/s106/tess-s0106-1-2_341.971994_-33.857307_1x1_astrocut.fits (Oct 19 21:21) has TIC 206620592's coordinates. It predates this review and is recorded as disclosed in DECISIONS item 69 ('206620592 cutout disclosure').

The QLP camera/CCD equals the TESScut camera/CCD for S96 (2-4), S103 (4-4) and S105 (2-2). TESScut S105 lacks 71 FFIs that QLP has (67 after the last TESScut cadence), which is why S105 uses the gap-edge branch.

Evaluator runs (3 of the budget of 12): E1 with the correct clock record gives RECOVERED, joint offset -2 min, SNR 7.61; E2 with a wrong record gives RECOVERED, -6 min; E3 with --allow-no-clock gives RECOVERED, +2 min.

adversarial.summary:
I attacked scripts/prereg_conformance.py (conformance-v2.0, the unchanged script) in two ways. First, an in-process replica that calls the script's own coverage, red_noise_beta and event_grid functions and copies lines 118-191 word for word. Second, 10 real CLI runs that confirmed the hits (each took 2-7 s, not 30-60 s). Before using the replica I checked it against 5 of the authors' stored calibration JSONs: outcome, min-gate outcome, joint offset and SNR matched exactly. Any number marked MC comes from the replica. Any number marked CLI is real script output. No S106 photometry was read. S106 timing comes only from the schedule in catalogs/TESS_orbit_times.csv.

The evaluator can be made to return all three false outcomes on real in-sample QLP data:
- **False RECOVERED:** TIC 120444365 S105 with no signal.
- **False INCONSISTENT:** TIC 183374279 S105 with no signal.
- **False EXCLUDED:** TIC 183374279 S105 with real reference transits injected at the predicted times.

In all three, the predictions sit 0.4-1.0 d after the light curve resumes following an orbit gap, where ramps are present. The evaluator has no rule for segment edges or ramps. Several locked S106 epochs fall in this zone, including 120444365 epochs 562 and 563 and 183374279 epoch 246.

Synthetic cases at the real operating SNR show three more problems:
- The published validation was run at about 10x the real SNR. At the real SNR, the reviewers' counterexamples (opposite ±50 min, 0.6x and 1.5x durations) return RECOVERED in 5-50% of trials.
- A real but displaced transit returns EXCLUDED instead of INCONSISTENT 12-60% of the time.
- At high SNR, a real on-time transit with ±20% depth scatter between events returns AMBIGUOUS 57% of the time.

Stationary red noise, white-noise nulls, ordinary gaps, a trapezoid (ingress/egress) transit shape and 20+ event targets produced no false RECOVERED or INCONSISTENT. Power is low for the shallow, many-event targets. Working files are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fernando-Desktop-NASA/c3c861f6-d690-49d9-96f5-051efe8a7e34/scratchpad/wf_review/adversarial/: scripts in code/, CLI inputs and outputs in cli/ (*.json, *_lc.csv, *_pred.csv, *_cfg.json), MC tables in mc/ (mc_main.csv, mc2.csv, mc3.csv).
checks_done: Replica check: the in-process replica matched the authors' CLI outputs exactly (outcome, min-gate outcome, joint offset, SNR) on 5 stored cases: conf_calib2_0/183374279_S105_null_0.3112, conf_calib2_1/120444365_S105_inject_0.3840, conf_calib2_2/120444365_S96_null_0.2963, conf_calib2_1/120444365_S105_null_0.7043, conf_calib2_0/183374279_S105_inject_0.6284.

White-noise nulls at the operating SNR (1200 ppm, 200-s cadence, 1000 ppm / 2 h reference): 0/120 false RECOVERED and 0/120 false INCONSISTENT (2, 3 and 6 events). No false RECOVERED or INCONSISTENT in 0/30 nulls each for the 206620592-like (24 events), 115692561-like (30 events) and 122522485-like (12 events) setups.

Control (reference transit on time) at the operating SNR: RECOVERED 37/40, 40/40 and 40/40 (2, 3, 6 events); 0 INCONSISTENT. High-SNR 253931796-like control: 30/30; trapezoid shape (20% ingress/egress): 30/30; 1.2x duration: 30/30.

Stationary AR(1) red noise (tau 1 h / 400 ppm and 4 h / 500 ppm, on 1200 ppm white noise): the red-noise factor beta engaged (1.52-1.76). 0/160 false RECOVERED or INCONSISTENT. Std of null depth/err at the predicted time: 0.99-1.34.
Displaced +200 min at reference depth: INCONSISTENT 40/40 with 6 events and 35/40 with 3 events (correct in that regime; see the EXCLUDED finding for fewer events and shallower dips).
Timing just outside the gate: true offsets of 40 and 50 min were rarely RECOVERED (at most 2/40 and 1/40).
Fully duration-mismatched transits (1.8x) at the operating SNR: RECOVERED at most 1/40.
Systematics in a many-event target: 24 events, 2 of them carrying a 4x-reference 3-h dip at +100 min, gave 0/30 false RECOVERED or INCONSISTENT.

Gap and eligibility attacks (in-process): events missing one baseline side are correctly ineligible; data only within ±0.5 d islands of each event works (19/20 RECOVERED); no false outcome from gap placement on its own.
V-shaped grazing eclipse (analytic only, not run): the optimal box is 2/3 of T14 with 2/3 of the depth, so it stays inside the 0.7-1.3 duration band and 0.5-1.5 depth range. Not an attack vector.
Error calibration on the authors' nulls: round-2 std of depth/err at the predicted time is 0.84-1.16. Round 1 for 183374279 is overdispersed (std 2.49, max |z| 5.2, n=9).
Clock gate not tested (other reviewers' dimension). All attack inputs used product 'synthetic' with CSV light curves, which bypasses the gate by design.

No S106 or later photometry was read. S106 segment timing came only from catalogs/TESS_orbit_times.csv. Nothing inside /Users/fernando/Desktop/NASA was written. 10 CLI runs were used out of the 12 allowed.

statistics.summary:
I recomputed every rate from the six calibration summary.csv files, and they match the draft document and DECISIONS 72-73 exactly. I made 12 evaluator runs: 5 re-runs of the authors' saved inputs and 6 new displaced-injection tests on in-sample data, plus 1 duplicate re-run. The numbers are honest. What they are claimed to show is not.

(1) Calibration covers only 2 of the 7 S106 tests: TIC 183374279 and 120444365, both with a 30-min gate and joint SNR of about 6-9. Using the evaluator's own preprocessing on noise already on disk, I estimate that a reference-depth transit in S106 gives joint SNR of only about 3-4 for TIC 115692561 and 122522485. That is below the RECOVERED threshold even with no noise. TIC 253931796 has S of about 32-40, so a null there would almost certainly come out EXCLUDED. The blanket statements ("RECOVERED about 90%", "1 in 50 false", "EXCLUDED rarely reachable") are therefore wrong for several tests.

findings.evidence: Synthetic, 70441745-like (ref 1829 ppm / 1.5 h, sigma 43.4, both dips at +120 min): conformance RECOVERED (local band fit +118 min, SNR 119.8). Its own stack_at_prediction is -34 ± 15 ppm, which meets the EXCLUDED condition (-34 + 45 < 549), but RECOVERED takes precedence (wf_review/faithfulness/syn/w70_off120.json). The frozen evaluator on the same light curve gives EXCLUDED (frozen_w70.json). Real noise (70441745 in-sample S96 SAP, reference dips injected at +100 min): conformance RECOVERED (band +98 min, SNR 10.7). Fixed-phase depth there is 41 ± 184 ppm (SNR 0.2); the EXCLUDED condition is not met in this run (41 + 552 = 593 > 549). Frozen evaluator: EXCLUDED (null70/inj_off100_ph0.30.json, frozen_inj_off100.json). Scope: 70441745 has zero overlap for 45 < |o| <= 130 min. For 253931796 (T14/2 = 132 vs gate ~135.5) zero overlap occurs only at 132-135.5 min, and at 120 min the fixed-phase depth is still ~0.55 of the dip. 122522485 is unaffected (gate 48 < 66). The registration wording 'within ±3 sigma of ≥2 predicted times' does not rescue this: the addenda name the frozen evaluator, which measures depth at the predicted time. The written RECOVERED and INCONSISTENT clauses also overlap for 30 < |o| <= 130 min, and the code settles that in favour of RECOVERED without saying so.

State the RECOVERED/INCONSISTENT overlap for sigma > 10 min objects and how it is resolved. Re-run the calibration (in-sample proxy: about the same power, see the max-statistic finding).

votes.reason:
The finding's factual core holds, and I reproduced it. For TIC 70441745 (sigma 43.4 min, so the gate is 130.2 min; T14 is 1.5 h, so T14/2 is 45 min), prereg_conformance.py scores RECOVERED a pair of dips at +120 min that do not overlap the predicted in-transit interval at all. The frozen prereg_test.py scores the same light curve EXCLUDED. The divergence comes from one place only: where the depth is measured. The frozen evaluator's own timing check passes (mean box offset 118.8 <= 130.2) and its fitted box depth is 1825 ppm (about 1.0x ref). It rejects RECOVERED only because it uses the depth at the unshifted predicted phase, which is what PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:42 specifies.

The conformance evaluator moves the RECOVERED depth to the fitted offset. Under the protocol's measurement, the 130-min gate cannot be reached beyond |o| = T14/2 = 45 min. Under the conformance evaluator it can. This widens RECOVERED, in the direction that favours the authors' hypothesis. It is not among the five frozen-evaluator defects the conformance document says it fixes (CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md:5-10). It is also untested: every synthetic case uses sigma 2.1 min (gate 30 min, below T14/2), and the calibration used only objects with a 30-min gate. So the behaviour is neither declared as a departure nor tested in the large-sigma regime.

Parts of the finding are weaker than stated:
(1) The registration's own RECOVERED clause, "a box of depth 0.5-1.5x ... within +-3 sigma_min of >= 2 predicted times" (PREREGISTRATION_v2.md:15-16), contrasts with its EXCLUDED clause, "stacked depth at the predicted phase". That supports the shifted-box reading the conformance code uses.
(2) The addendum at line 22 cites the frozen evaluator only for the timing-offset gate. Its depth-location rule does not come with it.
(3) An earlier review (REVIEW_timing_rule.md:384) said the frozen evaluator's EXCLUDED for a displaced dip "is code behavior, not proof that the broad prose uniquely prescribes this label". So calling the frozen EXCLUDED the 'governing' result overstates it, although the protocol text (line 38) does name the frozen script.
(4) The frozen -829 ppm depth at the predicted time is an artefact: the displaced dip falls inside its 0.75-1.5 T14 linear-baseline window. The true depth at the predicted phase is about 0 ppm (-39 and -4 ppm by direct median; the conformance stack gives -34 +- 15 ppm). So EXCLUDED is met on the merits, but not by the frozen number.
(5) The claim of 'zero overlap for 45 < |o| <= 130' is wrong. Zero overlap starts at |o| >= T14 = 90 min. For 45-90 min the overlap is partial, with fixed-phase depth below 0.5x. For 253931796 (T14 264 min) zero overlap never occurs inside the gate; the fixed-phase depth only falls just below 0.5x at 132-135.5 min.
(6) The claim that the code 'settles [the overlap] without saying so' is partly false. The docstring (lines 33-37) and the procedure document (line 35) state the precedence and that INCONSISTENT needs |o| > max(gate, 30). What is missing is any statement that this departs from the protocol's '> 30 min' INCONSISTENT text and its depth-at-predicted-time rule.

Severity: major rather than blocker. The behaviour can be defended from the registration wording and from the publicly adopted 130.2-min gate. The required fix is to declare and justify this departure (and add a large-sigma synthetic case) before publication. A fixed-phase requirement is one option, not the only one; and adding it would make the adopted max() gate inoperative beyond T14/2. It must still be done before any S106 data are examined, and it materially affects one object (70441745) and one only marginally (253931796).

The behaviour itself reproduces. With dips at +120 min, the conformance evaluator returns RECOVERED and the frozen evaluator returns EXCLUDED. What does not hold up is the claim that this is a blocker defect against a governing procedure that gives EXCLUDED.

1. The frozen EXCLUDED is an artefact, not a measurement of "no dip". The frozen baseline (prereg_test.py:38-40) uses points 0.75-1.5 T14 from tc, and a dip displaced by +120 min sits on that baseline. The stacked depth then comes out strongly negative: -1200±137 ppm (-8.7 sigma) synthetic, -650±159 ppm on real S96 noise. The conformance stack_at_prediction that "meets the EXCLUDED condition" has the same contamination (prereg_conformance.py:102-105, ±3D baseline): -404±154 and -295±185 ppm.

2. The frozen evaluator cannot be the reference for RECOVERED timing on this object. Its depth-at-predicted-time reading fails to recover a reference-depth transit only +30 min late (AMBIGUOUS, depth 744±137, 0.41x ref). That is below the protocol's own 30-min floor, never mind the 130.2-min tolerance it reports. Its outputs are also non-monotonic: +45 INCONSISTENT, then +60/+90/+120 EXCLUDED. Calling a strong SNR 9-14 dip EXCLUDED ("no signal") contradicts the protocol's own Inconsistent clause, which describes exactly this case (PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:51-52, "ephemeris wrong, signal real").

3. The object's registration defines RECOVERED by a box position, not by phase. PREREGISTRATION_v2.md:15-16 reads "a box of depth 0.5-1.5x and duration 0.7-1.3x ... within ±3 sigma_min of >= 2 predicted times". It reserves "stacked depth at the predicted phase" for EXCLUDED only (line 17-18). The addendum at line 22 imports the frozen evaluator's timing gate, which CLARIFICATION:58 spells out as a formula. It does not import the depth measurement. A 120-min offset with sigma 43.4 is a 2.8-sigma timing deviation, inside the adopted max() gate. It does not "miss" the predicted window once timing uncertainty is included.

4. "Without saying so" is false. Docstring lines 33-37 fix the precedence RECOVERED > INCONSISTENT > EXCLUDED, measure RECOVERED at the fitted offset with |o| <= gate, and require |o| > max(gate, 30) for INCONSISTENT. CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE lines 32-35 repeat this.

5. The real dispute is RECOVERED vs INCONSISTENT for 30 < |o| <= 130 min. That is the max()/min() timing question, already settled by the dated clarification. The min() reading is reported for every test, and it gives INCONSISTENT for these cases.

6. The proposed fix would cut the effective gate to about T14/2 and partly undo the adopted max() rule. Letting EXCLUDED take precedence when the predicted phase is empty would label a real transit 2.8 sigma late as EXCLUDED, through the baseline artefact in point 1.

Residual issue (minor): PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:42 does define "stacked depth" as the depth at the predicted time. The public procedure document's "Why" list does not name the switch to fitted-offset depth as a departure from the frozen evaluator. Nor does it say that for 70441745 and 253931796 RECOVERED can occur with no overlap at the nominal phase while the frozen output reads EXCLUDED. That deserves one disclosure sentence before publication. It is not a blocker.

findings.title: RECOVERED takes the maximum SNR over offsets and durations, not the protocol's depth at the predicted time (look-elsewhere boost, not flagged as a departure)

findings.evidence: Calculated from the authors' calibration JSONs (wf_review/faithfulness/fixed_phase.py). The median of local band SNR minus fixed-phase SNR is +1.75/+1.76 on nulls (rounds 1/2) but only +0.33/+0.37 on injections. Rounds 1+2 combined: conformance RECOVERED 2/100 nulls and 90/100 injections. A fixed-phase proxy (stack_at_prediction SNR >= 5 and depth 0.5-1.5x) gives 1/100 nulls and 91/100 injections, and the real in-sample transits pass it 3/3. The proxy has no separate timing check, so the protocol-literal false rate is at most the proxy's. Both null RECOVERED cases sit exactly at the gate edge (+30 and -30 min; widegate_lb.py output). The SNR >= 5 threshold was 'not tuned' (procedure doc l.78), but the statistic it applies to was changed.
findings.fix: Require the protocol's fixed-phase stacked depth/SNR in addition to the joint fit (no power cost in-sample), or state this as a departure and report the null/injection rates for both statistics.

votes.reason:
The code part of the finding is accurate. RECOVERED (scripts/prereg_conformance.py:181-184) uses best(loc, band). That is the highest joint SNR over offsets |o| <= max(gate,30)+T14/2 and durations 0.7-1.3x ref, and the result passes only if that best point falls inside the gate. The fixed-phase stack (line 179, offset 0, duration = ref) is used only for EXCLUDED (lines 188-189). The public protocol does define the stacked depth and SNR at the predicted time: PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:42 says "per covered transit, the depth at the predicted time ... stacked depth and offset weighted by inverse variance", and the frozen prereg_test.py:40,46 computes stacked_snr from depth_at_pred. I found no file that calls this change a departure. Both the docstring (line 4, "implements the written protocol outcome rules") and CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE l.78/86 ("the protocol's SNR >= 5") present it as the protocol statistic. I re-ran the reviewer's scripts and got every number exactly. The two false RECOVERED nulls sit at +30 and -30 min, and their fixed-phase SNRs are only 0.59 and 3.1, so the look-elsewhere boost is real.

I rate it minor rather than major, for four reasons:
(a) The per-object registrations for the S106 objects (120444365, 70441745 and 183374279 PREREGISTRATION_v2.md, the outcome-rule lines) define RECOVERED as "a box of depth 0.5-1.5x and duration 0.7-1.3x ... within +-3 sigma_min (and in any case within +-30 min) of >= 2 predicted times, stacked SNR >= 5". The same text restricts "at the predicted phase" to EXCLUDED. That reads as a local box search, so the change departs from the protocol's description of the frozen evaluator, not from every rule text.
(b) The protocol's duration test (0.7-1.3x) cannot be checked at a fixed reference duration, so some duration search is needed anyway.
(c) The false-RECOVERED rate of the statistic actually used was measured on 100 nulls and disclosed (2%). The fixed-phase proxy gives 1/100, a gap of one event.
(d) The fixed-phase depth and error are written to every output JSON.

The proposed fix also overstates one thing. Requiring the fixed-phase test in addition to the joint fit is not free in-sample: it lowers injection recovery from 90/100 to 84/100, and real injections from 3/3 to 2/3.

findings.title: INCONSISTENT: written per-event rule replaced by a common-offset, SNR>=7 rule; asymmetric with RECOVERED (SNR>=5) and changed after calibration
findings.location: scripts/prereg_conformance.py:36-38,187; PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:51-52; registrations l.18 ('its times differ by > 30 min from every prediction'); scripts/test_conformance.py:22; CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md:78
findings.evidence: The written rule is per-event: a comparable dip more than 30 min from every predicted time. The code needs one common offset across events, a joint SNR >= 7 and |o| > max(gate, 30). Incoherent displacements (for example a wrong period) can therefore never return INCONSISTENT; the opposite50 expectation was changed from INCONSISTENT to AMBIGUOUS after round-1 calibration. The look-elsewhere allowance was added only to this negative route, while RECOVERED also searches offsets and durations and keeps SNR 5 (2% false rate). A real but mistimed signal at SNR 5-7 is reported AMBIGUOUS rather than INCONSISTENT. This tilts away from a negative verdict. It is disclosed but not justified as an asymmetry.
findings.fix: State the asymmetry and why it is acceptable, or apply the same look-elsewhere treatment to both routes. Report per-event displaced-dip counts as a declared secondary readout so the written per-event INCONSISTENT clause is still checked.

votes.reason:
The core of the finding is literally true. The written INCONSISTENT clause has no SNR threshold. The code requires one common offset across events, joint SNR >= 7 and |o| > max(gate, 30 min). That route, and the removal of the per-event route, were changed after round-1 calibration. The opposite50 expectation was changed from INCONSISTENT to AMBIGUOUS at the same time. All of this is disclosed and was done before any test data were examined.

Four parts of the finding are overstated.
(1) "Incoherent displacements can never return INCONSISTENT" is false. My synthetic runs returned INCONSISTENT for offsets of +40/+60 min and for a 4-event drift from 40 to 90 min. Only spreads near or above about T14/2 fail, as in opposite50 (+-50 min with a 2 h duration). A wrong period large enough to break coherence within one sector would have to be hundreds to thousands of sigma_P away from the frozen value: about 1700 sigma_P for 120444365, about 2400 for 183374279 and about 240 for 70441745. So the "wrong period" example is not a realistic failure mode.
(2) The "written per-event rule" is ambiguous text. The protocol's INCONSISTENT clause says "a dip ... its time" (singular), against "stacked" in the RECOVERED clause. The registrations say "its times differ" (plural).
(3) "Not justified" is partly wrong. The docstring cites a look-elsewhere allowance for about 20-40 trials. The procedure document says RECOVERED keeps the protocol's written SNR >= 5 and was not tuned. Round-1 data support a larger trials factor for the +-0.3 d window: 3 of 49 nulls gave false INCONSISTENT from the joint route at SNR 5.1-5.75, against 1 of 49 false RECOVERED. What is missing is one explicit argument for the asymmetry.
(4) The direction of the "tilt" is arguable. INCONSISTENT asserts "signal real, ephemeris wrong". The removed routes produced false "signal real" claims on empty windows.

What does stand, and matters: the SNR >= 7 gate costs real power. In the authors' round-2 reference-depth injections, 20 of 51 had joint SNR below 7. A coherently mistimed real signal at the reference depth would therefore come out AMBIGUOUS about 39% of the time. RECOVERED power is about 90%. Two unambiguous per-event dips at SNR 65 each, 50 min off (opposite50), also give AMBIGUOUS, which contradicts the literal written clause. That conflicts with the docstring's claim that the evaluator implements the written rules.

Severity: minor. The issue cannot produce a false RECOVERED, and both outcomes are non-RECOVERED; the protocol (tex l.56) reports every non-Recovered outcome as such. It is disclosed, it was fixed before any test data were seen, and the scenario where it matters needs a >10-sigma timing failure for most targets. The fix is documentation: argue the asymmetry explicitly, and declare the per-event displaced count as a secondary readout. That count is already computed and written to the output JSON, but it is not declared.

votes.reason:
I could not refute it. Every behavioural claim reproduced with the real evaluator (6 runs out of the 12 allowed), and the file-reading claims check out. Part of the result is stronger than the finding says.

1. The joint SNR >= 7 gate decides between INCONSISTENT and AMBIGUOUS for a real, mistimed signal at the reference depth. I kept the same +200 min, 1000 ppm, 2 h signal and changed only the noise. At joint SNR 5.5 and 6.23 the result was AMBIGUOUS. At 7.26 and 11.33 it was INCONSISTENT. In all four runs the depth was comparable and the depths agreed across events (p >= 0.49), so SNR was the only thing that differed. In the round-2 calibration outputs, 19 of 51 eligible reference-depth injections have band SNR between 5 and 7. So a displaced real signal would come out INCONSISTENT about 61% of the time (31/51), while an on-time one is RECOVERED 90% of the time.

2. Displacements that are not the same at every event (for example a wrong period) never reach INCONSISTENT, and they come out EXCLUDED, not AMBIGUOUS. This happened with offsets of +100 and +250 min (per-event SNR 67 and 65), and with three events drifting +90, +180 and +270 min (per-event SNR 16-17). In both runs every event is flagged `displaced=True`. That is the case the protocol keeps INCONSISTENT for ("ephemeris wrong, signal real"), and the evaluator itself checks INCONSISTENT before EXCLUDED. A real signal is therefore reported in the wrong negative category. This is why I keep the severity at major.

3. The change after calibration is shown by the authors' backup files, not only by their decision log. `prereg_conformance_v2.0_precalib.py:187` returned INCONSISTENT for a comparable shifted fit with no SNR 7 requirement, or for 2 or more displaced events. The current line 187 dropped the per-event route and added SNR >= 7. The comment on line 186 still describes the per-event route the code no longer has. None of the three registrations has a dated amendment to the INCONSISTENT clause (it stands at lines 17, 18 and 21). The only commitment is CLARIFICATION_TIMING_RULE l.56, which points to a procedure document not yet published.

Where the finding overstates:
- **The written rule is not clearly per-event.** "A comparable dip ... its times differ by > 30 min from every prediction" can be read either way, though the per-event reading is the more natural one.
- **The asymmetry has a partial justification.** Docstring l.37 cites look-elsewhere for 20-40 trials. RECOVERED's SNR 5 is fixed by the protocol, and its search window is ±(gate + T14/2) against ±432 min for INCONSISTENT, so a trial-count argument exists even though it is not written as one.
- **"Tilts away from a negative verdict" is too simple.** INCONSISTENT claims the signal is real, so SNR >= 7 limits false "signal real" calls (12% of empty windows in round 1, 0/51 in round 2). Precedence also means it cannot create a RECOVERED. And the incoherent cases land on EXCLUDED, a harsher negative. The real defect is that outcomes are put in the wrong category, not a one-way tilt.
- **The second fix is partly in place.** Each event's `displaced` flag is already written to the output JSON, and procedure doc l.94 commits to reporting all per-transit numbers. It is labelled "for information only", though, not a declared check of the written clause.
- **Realism.** A displacement that differs between events within one sector needs a gross period error for σ = 2-3 min targets. It is more plausible for TIC 70441745, where σ = 43 min.

findings.title: Coverage rule redefines INSUFFICIENT and RECOVERED eligibility ('covered' 60% → 'fully covered' 90% + baselines); not flagged as a departure
findings.evidence: The protocol uses 'covered' (>=60% of cadences within ±1.5 T14) for RECOVERED and INSUFFICIENT, and 'fully covered' only for EXCLUDED. On the synthetic partial_one case the frozen evaluator counts 2 covered (epoch 2 coverage 0.81) and returns RECOVERED at SNR 70.6 (wf_review/faithfulness/frozen_partial_one.json). Conformance makes epoch 2 ineligible (cov_in 0.43) and returns INSUFFICIENT (conf_test/partial_one.json). The change defers tests rather than tilting toward a pass, but it is a written rule not implemented. The procedure doc (l.28) presents it without calling it a departure.
findings.fix: Declare it as a departure from PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:41, or use the protocol's 'covered' definition for INSUFFICIENT and the eligibility of RECOVERED, and full coverage only for EXCLUDED.

votes.reason:
I could not refute it, and each part checks out on reading. The protocol defines "covered" as at least 60% of cadences within ±1.5 durations (PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:41). RECOVERED and INSUFFICIENT use "covered" (tex:49, 54). Only EXCLUDED says "fully covered" (tex:53). The conformance evaluator uses a different test: at least 90% of the in-transit interval plus baselines of 0.5×T14 or more on each side (prereg_conformance.py:20-21, 70-77, 141). It then drops every event that fails this test from all outcomes (INSUFFICIENT at :158-159 if fewer than 2 pass). So a written rule for two outcomes was replaced, not just tightened for EXCLUDED.

Nothing I found declares this as a departure. The docstring (:4) says the evaluator "implements the written protocol outcome rules". The procedure document (l.28, l.33) states the full-coverage eligibility with no departure wording, and its list of the frozen evaluator's faults (l.9) names only the EXCLUDED coverage issue. The CLARIFICATION file (l.54) and DECISIONS items 71-73 say nothing about a change for RECOVERED or INSUFFICIENT. Only the internal review prompt (PROMPT_conformance_review.txt:31) lists "the coverage definition" as a deviation to check.

Mitigating points: the referee review (REVIEW_S106_test_procedure.md:55) recommended stricter eligibility, and the TIC 183374279 addendum (l.24) supports it for that one object. That is a justification, not a declaration, and it does not cover the other six configs.

One correction to the finding: the two definitions are not nested, so the change is not strictly conservative. In an edge case the conformance rule accepts an event that the protocol would not count as covered.

votes.reason:
I reproduced the finding. It is a real mismatch between what was committed and what the code does, not just loose wording. CLARIFICATION_TIMING_RULE l.18 promises "the individual-event assessment under min(3 sigma, 30 min)". The only min() outcome the evaluator reports is outcome_min_gate_reading (prereg_conformance.py l.191). That is the joint fit with one common offset across events, gated at min(3*mean(sigma_min), 30) (l.156). I ran synthetic cases with opposite offsets per event (injected -8/+8 and -12/+12 min, sigma 2.1, so the min() gate is 6.3 min). The joint min() reading came out RECOVERED in both: the fit found a common offset of 0 and widened the box to 2.3-2.4 h. Yet every event had match_min=False, because the per-event fitted offsets were -10/+7 and -13/+10 min, all beyond 6.3 min. So the published min() readout can say RECOVERED while the individual-event assessment is 0/2. The procedure doc (l.87) still says this reading is reported "as committed".

The strongest counter-argument is that events[].match_min is saved in the output JSON, and the procedure doc l.94 promises "all per-transit numbers". That does not rescue it, for three reasons:
(a) The criteria behind match_min are declared nowhere. They are a per-event SNR >= 3, a free 1-min offset grid over +-0.3 d and a duration search of 0.5-2.0x reference (l.80-83, l.148). The docstring l.31 says only "recorded for information", the procedure doc never mentions them, and the registration l.20 sets a stacked SNR >= 5, not a per-event threshold.
(b) Nothing combines the per-event flags into the "of >= 2 predicted times" count that the registration wording requires. My runs found no top-level output key for this.
(c) The clarification's own impact table treats the gate per event ("8.1–8.4 min" l.27; "134.4–136.5 per event" l.30), but the evaluator's min() outcome uses the mean sigma.

Why major rather than minor: the reported min() outcome can contradict the very commitment it claims to fulfil. Mitigations: the procedure doc has not been published yet (DECISIONS l.376, "awaiting external review"), and the fix is to declare the criteria, not to change any data. I did not check whether the wording of l.18 is already in the public v1.10 release, and the finding does not depend on that.

votes.reason:
The factual observation holds up. None of the four registrations mentions the conformance procedure, and the newest note in each still says the timing rule is "as implemented in the frozen evaluator scripts/prereg_test.py". The two claims that justify the "major" rating do not hold up.

(a) Holds. The four files contain no pointer to the conformance procedure, so someone who reads only those files would score the test with prereg_test.py alone. The same "frozen evaluator" sentence is in all 7 S106 registrations. 183374279 later contradicts it in its own amendment; 120444365 and 70441745 mention the conformance procedure only for the reference values.

(b) Refuted: "No document declares this replacement for these registrations." CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md l.12 says outcomes "will be assessed with the separately versioned conformance evaluator defined here". Its l.47-50 name each of the four tests (206620592, 122522485, 253931796, 115692561), each with a locked config. Each locked config's "evaluator" field names scripts/prereg_conformance.py. CLARIFICATION_TIMING_RULE_2026-10-20.md l.56 had already announced that a separate conformance procedure and its precedence would be fixed and published before inspection. One caveat: DECISIONS.md item 73 (l.376) says the procedure document is still "awaiting external review before publication", and it sits in results/, not next to the registrations.

(c) Refuted: "the per-event depth/duration clause was replaced". The registration clause names a single box ("a box of depth 0.5-1.5x ... of >= 2 predicted times") and a "stacked SNR >= 5". The governing protocol (PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex l.49) says "stacked depth between 0.5 and 1.5 times the reference", and the frozen evaluator also tests stacked depth (prereg_test.py l.6, l.49). The conformance evaluator tests the stacked depth (prereg_conformance.py l.177, function comparable). Its l.164 adds per-event checks (chi2 p >= 0.01, Npos >= 2) that neither the protocol nor the frozen evaluator required. That makes the rule stricter, not looser, and the change is declared in CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE l.29-30.

So the finding is a cross-reference gap, not an undeclared rule change. Severity drops to minor. The proposed fix, a dated note in all 7 registrations naming the procedure and its precedence, is still sensible housekeeping, but it should not describe the change as replacing per-event depth matching.

The code mechanics are as described and the numbers reproduce. What does not hold up is the claim that this is a blocker in the conformance evaluator, and the premise behind it, that the protocol does not tie exclusion to the nominal time.
(1) Testing at offset 0 is the registered rule. PREREGISTRATION_v2.md:17 for this very object says "(3) excluded - stacked depth at the predicted phase < 0.3x at 3 sigma". PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:42 defines the stacked depth as "per covered transit, the depth at the predicted time (local linear baseline) ... stacked ... weighted by inverse variance", and line 53 uses that quantity. The frozen evaluator does the same (prereg_test.py:38-40,50). The conformance docstring (:39) and the procedure doc (:36) state "at the predicted times" openly. The proposed max-over-gate rule would be a new, stricter EXCLUDED rule, not a conformance fix.
(2) Most of the displaced-dip EXCLUDED rate comes from the registered rule, not from baseline bias. With a baseline taken outside the timing window, a 0.3x dip at +100 min still passes the EXCLUDED test 62% of the time, the same as the null. Its true box depth at the predicted phase is 0, so under the registration EXCLUDED is the correct literal outcome. The median-baseline bias only raises that rate from 62% to 77%.
(3) The registered method is more biased than the conformance one. The local linear baseline (+-1.5 D window) gives -310, -446 and -945 ppm for the 0.3x, 0.45x and 1.0x dips at +100 min, against -126, -180 and -320 ppm for the conformance median. The conformance evaluator reduces the effect the finding objects to.
(4) The bias cannot turn an on-time signal of at least 0.3x into EXCLUDED (0.3x on time: 0/100). A reference-depth dip inside the gate is RECOVERED first by precedence.
What remains is a protocol-level limitation that should be disclosed. For TIC 70441745 the gate (130 min) exceeds T14 (90 min), so a sub-threshold dip displaced within the gate can come out EXCLUDED rather than AMBIGUOUS. That calls for a stated caveat, not a blocker.

I could not refute it. Every behaviour in the finding reproduced. EXCLUDED is computed only at offset 0 with D = ref (prereg_conformance.py:178-179 sets stack_at_prediction = Sd[i0, j_ref]; :188-189 tests depth + 3 err < 0.3 ref). Each event's baseline is the median of all points with D/2 <= |x| < 3D (:102). For TIC 70441745 the gate is 130.2 min and T14/2 is 45 min, so a dip the registration allows (+100 min) falls completely outside the offset-0 box and lands inside its baseline window. That pulls the offset-0 stack negative and makes EXCLUDED more likely than under the null. Running the unmodified CLI on one noise realisation with a 0.6x-ref dip at +100 min gives EXCLUDED under the adopted max() gate. Its own local_max band fit in the same JSON is a VALID, consistent (p = 0.86) 899 ppm dip at SNR 5.4 at +98 min. The same noise with the dip on time gives RECOVERED. So the verdict contradicts the evaluator's own fit inside the registered gate.

One correction to the finding's framing: it says the protocol (tex:53) does not restrict exclusion to the nominal time. But PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:41-42 defines the per-transit depth as "the depth at the predicted time (local linear baseline)". The frozen prereg_test.py:38-41 and :50 does the same, and its baseline is a linear fit over 0.75-1.5 D, which a displaced dip would also contaminate. So testing EXCLUDED only at offset 0 follows the protocol. The flaw comes from the written protocol and was not introduced by the conformance rewrite. Fixing it is therefore a dated protocol amendment, not a conformance correction. The behaviour is still wrong for a falsification verdict, because the protocol's own RECOVERED rule accepts offsets up to the gate.

Scope: in the 7 locked S106 configs, gate > T14/2 holds only for TIC 70441745 (130.2 vs 45 min) and, barely, TIC 253931796 (135.5 vs 132 min). The others have gate 30-48 min against T14/2 of 30-85 min.

Severity: blocker for the procedure as declared (this is my judgement). A falsification outcome that can contradict the evaluator's own in-gate fit should not be published as the declared method. The rate is about 1/100 at reference depth, 7/100 at 0.7x and 20/100 at 0.6x for a +100 min offset. Major is the lowest defensible rating given that the flaw comes from the protocol.

findings.title: EXCLUDED uses a plain inverse-variance stack with no per-event consistency check (asymmetric with RECOVERED's VALID gate)
findings.evidence: VALID (line 164) requires chi2 p >= 0.01 and >= 2 positive events for RECOVERED/INCONSISTENT, but EXCLUDED uses Sd[i0, j_ref] whatever the consistency. Authors' conf_real 183374279_S105_null_halfphase.json: EXCLUDED from per-event at-prediction depths -52 +- 240 and -1572 +- 241 ppm (chi2 19.94, dof 1, p = 8.0e-6), so one negative artifact decides the outcome. R6: a 0.5x-reference transit present in both events is EXCLUDED because of one artifact event (-1025 ppm). The test suite's 'brightening' case (both events) shows the design intent, but a single-event brightening or artifact is not covered.
findings.fix: Require EXCLUDED to pass a consistency test too: per-event chi2 p >= 0.01 at the evaluated point, or a robust stack (median of per-event depths, or leave-one-out: EXCLUDED only if every leave-one-out stack also satisfies the rule). Otherwise return AMBIGUOUS. Add a synthetic case 'dip at event 1 plus brightening/artifact at event 2' with a declared expectation.

votes.reason:
The finding holds. I read the declared version of the file: its SHA-256 is 0520ea58..., which matches CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md:17. In that file, VALID (line 164: ok_all & Sd>0 & Pc>=0.01 & Npos>=2) is used only to build Sn (line 165), and Sn feeds only best(), which serves the RECOVERED and INCONSISTENT checks (lines 184 and 187). stack_at_prediction is the plain inverse-variance stack Sd[i0, j_ref] (line 179, from Sd at line 162) with no VALID mask, and EXCLUDED (line 189) reads it directly. So EXCLUDED has no per-event consistency check while RECOVERED does. The docstring (lines 4 and 39) and the procedure doc (line 36) state the EXCLUDED rule as it is coded, so this is a design weakness, not a mismatch between documentation and code. The protocol (PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:53) also defines EXCLUDED as a plain stacked-depth rule. But the authors already added a consistency gate to RECOVERED, which the protocol does not require, so the asymmetry is theirs.

I checked the cited real-data case and the R6 claim and both reproduce. The strongest new point: the declared test one_dip_only (test_conformance.py:26) expects AMBIGUOUS. Adding a brightening at event 2 to that same setup flips the outcome to EXCLUDED, so making one event brighter turns a declared AMBIGUOUS into an exclusion claim. The test suite only covers a brightening at both events (line 30). It has no case mixing a dip at one event with a brightening or excursion at the other.

On severity, I grade it major, not blocker. With real noise, a full-depth transit at both events of TIC 183374279 would need a single-event excursion of about -2.5k ppm to be EXCLUDED; the in-sample excursion was -1572. So the realistic failure is sub-reference signals, or very large single-event excursions, being falsely EXCLUDED, as in R6, rather than a clear transit being misclassified. That is still a false public exclusion claim. RECOVERED is not affected, and per-event numbers are reported.

I did not verify where the -1572 ppm event comes from, so I call it a single-event negative excursion, not an artifact. In that event's window there is a separate 6474 ppm dip (SNR 28.7) at +154 min, with nothing comparable in the other event.

votes.reason:
I reproduced every part of the claim, and the code reading confirms it. VALID at scripts/prereg_conformance.py:164 requires Pc >= 0.01 and Npos >= 2, and that gate only applies to RECOVERED and INCONSISTENT through Sn (line 165). The EXCLUDED test (line 189) reads stack_at_prediction, which is the raw inverse-variance Sd/Se at [i0, j_ref] (lines 162 and 179), and nothing checks consistency there. When one event is anomalous, VALID fails everywhere, so the precedence falls through to EXCLUDED and one event decides the outcome. That holds even when the other event shows a strong dip at the predicted time.

Against the finding:
- The protocol defines Excluded only as 'stacked depth below 0.3 times the reference at 3σ' (PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:53), so the evaluator follows the protocol word for word. But the conformance evaluator already adds a consistency gate beyond the protocol text for RECOVERED, so the asymmetry is its own design choice.
- In the calibration, reference-depth (1.0x) injections never came out EXCLUDED (0 of 120). So the failure needs a transit below the reference depth or an artifact larger than the one seen in S105.
- The proposed p >= 0.01 gate has a cost: 5 of the 20 calibration null runs that came out EXCLUDED had per-event p < 0.01, so the fix would turn them into AMBIGUOUS.

None of this refutes the defect. A false EXCLUDED of a real 0.5x transit happens on real in-sample data, and on synthetic data a full-depth dip seen at SNR of about 55 is EXCLUDED.

findings.title: Red-noise beta is MAD-based, floored at 1, and measured at one timescale; it does not engage on real data with heavy-tailed or correlated noise
findings.location: scripts/prereg_conformance.py:61-68 (red_noise_beta), used at :89/:105 for all durations 0.5-2.0 x ref
findings.evidence: In-process replication of lines 129-138 on in-sample QLP SAP, 25 random pseudo-prediction sets, null centres. 183374279 S105: beta used = 1.000 in all 25 trials (unfloored MAD ratio 0.84 at T14), but the std-of-bin-means ratio is 5.9 and null z = dep/err at offset 0 / D=ref has std 5.13, with 11.4% |z| > 3; excluding centres < 1 d from segment edges, std is 1.19. 120444365 S105: beta in 1.00-1.25; null z std 1.49 at D=ref and 2.03 at D=2xref, frac |z| > 3 = 4.3% / 7.4%. 120444365 S96: z std 1.30 at D=ref, 1.77 at 2xref, frac |z| > 3 = 4.9% / 8.8%. Gaussian expectation is 0.27%. Because longer boxes are under-errored more, J_any (any duration) SNR is inflated relative to band fits, which biases comparable()'s delta-chi2 <= 4 duration test. beta also silently returns 1.0 when fewer than 8 bins exist (line 66; not triggered by the current configs).
findings.fix: Estimate beta per duration on the grid (or at least at 0.5, 1 and 2 x ref, taking the maximum), with a non-MAD scatter of bin means (e.g. std after 5-sigma clipping), or calibrate errors empirically from null positions in the same light curve, which the calibration machinery already supports. Record unfloored beta values and the bin count in the output, and flag when fewer than 8 bins are available instead of silently using 1.0.

votes.reason:
The code does what the finding says. In scripts/prereg_conformance.py, red_noise_beta (lines 61-68) takes 1.4826 x MAD of bin means, floors the result at 1, and bins only at the reference duration. It also returns 1.0 with no warning when fewer than 8 bins exist (line 66). Main computes this one beta once (line 137) and passes it to box_fit (line 89) and event_grid (line 105) for every duration from 0.5 to 2.0 x ref.

I re-ran the evaluator's own functions in-process on the S105/S96 light curves already on disk. Beta stays near 1 while the noise in scorable events is clearly larger than the errors assume, and the gap grows with box duration on all three light curves. So the main claim holds.

The finding overstates one thing. Its headline figure (null z std 5.13, 11.4% with |z| > 3) does not reproduce under the evaluator's coverage/eligibility gate. Under the gate I get about 1.9, so on the worst light curve the errors are too small by about 2x, not 5x. The 5.13 most likely comes from centres the evaluator would never score; my ungated run gives 3.30 at D=ref and 4.93 at 2 x ref.

Most of the excess comes from detrending ramps near segment edges. Dropping centres within 1 d of an edge brings the z std down to 1.05-1.17 on all three light curves.

How the too-small errors affect each outcome rule:
- The comparable() duration test (line 177) fails more often, which pushes results toward AMBIGUOUS. That direction is conservative.
- The SNR >= 5 RECOVERED threshold (line 184) and the SNR >= 7 INCONSISTENT threshold (line 187) are passed too easily.
- The EXCLUDED test, depth + 3*err < 0.3*ref (line 189), is also passed too easily when a real but weak signal is present.

Severity stays major. The authors' calibration found about 2% false RECOVERED (1/49 and 1/51, DECISIONS.md items 72-73), but that covers only 2 of the 7 S106 targets. Both null RECOVERED cases sit just over the threshold, which is what this error inflation would produce. The 5 uncalibrated targets include the shallowest, 115692561 (143 ppm) and 206620592 (287 ppm).

The proposed fix (a beta from the plain standard deviation of bin means) would over-correct: on 183374279 S105 that ratio is 3.2-6.0, which would inflate errors everywhere, including the well-behaved interior.

votes.reason:
I reproduced the claim. The code reading is correct: beta is MAD-based, floored at 1, and measured at one bin size (the reference duration). Lines 89 and 105 then apply that single beta to every duration from 0.5 to 2.0 x ref. When I rebuilt the evaluator's preprocessing in-process, beta stayed at about 1 even though the plain std-of-bin-means ratio is about 5.9 for TIC 183374279 S105. The null z-scores are far wider than Gaussian, and more so for longer boxes, which matches the finding.

The finding names the wrong main cause, though, and its proposed fix would not be enough. Most of the excess comes from events within 1 d of a segment edge, where the light curve ramps. Away from edges, null z std is only about 1.0-1.2 at D=ref (1.19-1.49 at 2 x ref). Near edges, z reaches 28. The fix the finding proposes (5-sigma-clipped std of bin means) gives a beta of only about 1.3, so a z=28 edge event would still be about z=21. A better beta number cannot absorb the edge ramps. What would work is screening events by distance from segment edges, or calibrating errors empirically from null positions in the same light curve.

The edge problem is also behind both false RECOVERED results in the authors' own calibration. In each case the edge event has the largest per-event depth, beta is 1.0, and the consistency p-value is barely above the 0.01 cut. So the consistency check is not a dependable backstop here. The coverage rule (lines 75-76) also accepted an event 0.13 d from a segment edge, so the eligibility step does not screen these out either.

The finding is right that longer boxes are under-errored more, which biases the delta-chi2 <= 4 duration test. That bias makes the outcome more likely to be AMBIGUOUS (fewer RECOVERED and INCONSISTENT), so it does not create false positives. The silent return of 1.0 below 8 bins (line 66) is confirmed by reading only; the current configs never trigger it (83-462 bins).

Severity: major. This error-model failure explains both empirical false RECOVERED results, the backstop nearly failed in both, and the evaluator has not been published yet, so it can still be fixed. In mitigation, the authors already disclose the roughly 2% empirical false-RECOVERED rate, and the output records every per-event number.

findings.title: Clock record is not validated against the config, light curve or predictions; any record is silently applied
findings.evidence: Only ck['event_btjd'] and ck['correction_min'] are read. The tic, sector, qlp_sha256 and event list in the record are never compared with cfg, sha(--lc) or pred.tc_btjd. Run R3b: config TIC 1 / product QLP / S106 with a clock JSON {tic: 999, sector: 50, qlp_sha256: '000...', event_btjd: [0, 1], correction_min: [500, 500]} is accepted. The output records the clock path and hash, clock_correction_min_range is [500, 500], and the outcome flips from RECOVERED (R3a, same light curve) to EXCLUDED. np.interp also silently returns wrong values if event_btjd is unsorted: xp=[4250, 4238, 4245], fp=[3, 1, 2] gives [3, 3, 2] instead of [1, 2, 3].
findings.fix: Before applying: require ck['tic'] == cfg['tic'], ck['sector'] == cfg['sector'], ck['qlp_sha256'] == sha(a.lc), and that ck['event_btjd'] equals the filtered pred.tc_btjd (same length, allclose), sorted ascending, with finite corrections. Otherwise return INVALID_INPUT (clock record mismatch).

votes.reason: I re-read the code and the claim holds as written; I also reproduced it. At scripts/prereg_conformance.py:125-127 the evaluator loads the clock JSON, records only its path and SHA-256, and reads only ck['event_btjd'] and ck['correction_min'] (np.interp(t, ev_t, ev_c)). Nothing compares the record's tic, sector, qlp_sha256 or event list with cfg, sha(a.lc) or the filtered pred.tc_btjd. The light curve itself does get such checks against the config (lines 112, 116, 117), but the clock record gets none. I used a synthetic CSV light curve and a QLP/S106 config (TIC 1); no test-sector data were opened. The same light curve gave RECOVERED with a matching zero-correction record. With the bogus record {tic 999, sector 50, qlp_sha256 0...0, event_btjd [0,1], correction_min [500,500]} it was accepted (exit 0) and gave EXCLUDED. The unsorted np.interp problem is real and does affect the evaluator's output. The fields the proposed fix needs (tic, sector, qlp_sha256, event_btjd) are written by qlp_clock_test_sector.py:37-39 and are present in every real S105 clock record in conf_real/. The producer (line 35) and the evaluator (line 119) use the same prediction filter, so the proposed allclose check on event_btjd can be met. Mitigations I found: (1) the docstring (step 1, lines 15-16) and CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE step 2 never promise clock-record validation, so this is a design gap, not a mismatch between docs and code. (2) All 7 locked S106 configs have predictions sorted ascending, and the producer writes event_btjd in that order, so an unsorted record cannot come from the declared pipeline, only from a hand-edited or wrong record. (3) The output records the clock path, its hash and the correction range, so someone who opens both files can catch a mismatch afterwards, but the evaluator itself never refuses. I still rate it major. findings.title: CSV light-curve path bypasses the declared header validation (sector, TIC) and the QUALITY/finite filtering, and is not recorded as such
findings.evidence: For --lc *.csv, sector and tic are copied from the config, so the line-116 check can never fail. There is no QUALITY filter and no finite filter: f / np.median(f) with one NaN gives an all-NaN array (verified). Runs R3a/R3b scored a CSV against a product='QLP', S106 config with no indication in the output that header checks were skipped. The docstring (lines 10, 15) promises FITS input and header validation.
findings.fix: Accept CSV only behind an explicit flag (e.g. --synthetic-csv) allowed only when cfg['product'] == 'synthetic', or refuse it. Record lc_format and 'header_checks': 'skipped' in res. Apply finite filtering if CSV is kept.

The code facts in the finding are correct. They do not support a "major" rating, so I rate it minor. Confirmed: for --lc *.csv, line 114 copies sector and TIC from the config, so the line-116 check can never fail. That branch has no QUALITY filter and no finite filter. The docstring (lines 10 and 15) declares FITS input and header validation, and the procedure document (step 1) declares a sector/TIC check. R3a/R3b used configs with product "QLP" and sector 106, and their output has no field saying header checks were skipped.

Three parts of the finding are overstated:
(1) "Not recorded as such" is only half true. Every run's output records the input path ("lc": "...csv") and lc_sha256, so an auditor can see the input was a CSV and not the MAST FITS file. Only an explicit lc_format / header_checks flag is missing.
(2) A single NaN does make the flux all-NaN, but the run then crashes at the detrending step (wotan ValueError, no output JSON). It fails loudly instead of silently giving a wrong score.
(3) The clock gate still applies on the CSV path: line 123 reads product and sector from the config, so a QLP S106 CSV is still refused without --clock.

Under the declared procedure the S106 input is a FITS file, which goes through load_lc: header SECTOR/TICID read, finite and QUALITY==0 mask at line 58. So the CSV path changes no S106 outcome unless the operator departs from the declared input, and that departure would show in the recorded path and hash. Proposed fix (gate CSV input behind product=="synthetic", record lc_format and header_checks, add a finite filter) is reasonable hardening.

Side issue I noticed: validate_conformance_real.py writes CSVs and runs them against product="QLP" configs. It repeats the QUALITY/finite filtering itself (line 18), which means the real-data validation never exercises the declared FITS loader. That is a test-coverage gap, separate from this finding.

findings.title: --allow-no-clock bypasses the declared clock gate for QLP sectors >= 99 without restriction and leaves no trace in the output
findings.evidence: The help text says 'ONLY for synthetic/self-tests or sectors < 99', but it is not enforced, and for sectors < 99 the gate does not apply anyway, so the flag only matters in the case it should never be used. Run R3a (product QLP, S106, --allow-no-clock): outcome RECOVERED; output has clock_correction_min_range [0, 0], no clock_record and no key mentioning the bypass. Run R4 (FITS, TIC 70441745 config, --allow-no-clock): RECOVERED, again with no bypass record. The docstring (line 12) says 'Without it the evaluator REFUSES to score'.
findings.fix: Allow the flag only when cfg['product'] == 'synthetic' (or the sector is < 99), otherwise refuse. Always write res['allow_no_clock'] = a.allow_no_clock and append '(CLOCK NOT APPLIED)' to the outcome string when it is used.

The finding holds as written. In scripts/prereg_conformance.py, line 110 defines --allow-no-clock with the help text "ONLY for synthetic/self-tests or sectors < 99", and nothing in the code checks that restriction. The gate at line 123 only runs when cfg["sector"] >= 99 and the product starts with "QLP". So for sectors below 99, and for product="synthetic" (the setting test_conformance.py uses), the flag changes nothing. Its only effect is to skip the refusal at line 124 for QLP sectors >= 99, which is exactly the case the help text excludes. Neither of the project's own scripts uses the flag: test_conformance.py relies on product="synthetic", and validate_conformance_real.py passes --clock for sectors >= 99. The docstring at lines 11-12 (named as the authoritative procedure), results/CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md line 26 and logs/DECISIONS.md line 362 all describe an unconditional refusal and never mention the flag. When the flag is used, the output has no key recording it.

One small overstatement: "no trace" is not quite right. The output JSON keeps the config (sector 106, product QLP) and has no clock_record key. Without the flag that combination can only give CLOCK_UNVERIFIED, so a careful auditor could work out that the gate was skipped. But nothing records it explicitly. The clock range [0,0] with no clock_record looks exactly like a legitimate sector < 99 run (the authors' S96 outputs show the same pattern).

I rate this minor rather than major. The flag has to be passed on purpose. The S105 clock corrections were only about 1.7 to 4.4 minutes, against a timing gate of at least 30 minutes. The published procedure also commits to reporting the clock record, so a missing record would be visible. Still, it is a real mismatch between the declared procedure and the code, and the proposed fix is reasonable.

findings.title: TIC header check silently passes when TICID is absent or 0; non-numeric OBJECT crashes
findings.evidence: load_lc on synthetic FITS: no TICID and no OBJECT gives tic=0; TICID=0 gives tic=0. In both cases (tic and tic != cfg['tic']) is False and the check is skipped. Full run R4: a FITS with no TICID scored RECOVERED against cfg tic 70441745, and the output records no TIC. OBJECT='Target' or 'TIC999' raises ValueError. Real QLP S105 files carry TICID in the primary header (verified), so the practical risk is low, but the declared step-1 guarantee does not hold in this branch.
findings.fix: Require a positive TIC: read TICID from the primary or ext-1 header, else parse OBJECT with a regex r'TIC\s*(\d+)'; if none is found, return INVALID_INPUT. Always write header_tic and header_sector into res.

findings.title: Zero matching predictions returns INSUFFICIENT instead of INVALID_INPUT; with a clock record it crashes
findings.evidence: R5a: prediction CSV with tess_sector 'S106' gives n_predicted 0 and outcome INSUFFICIENT (a scored category). R5b: the same with a clock record whose event list is empty gives ValueError 'array of sample points is empty' from np.interp at line 127.
findings.fix: If n_predicted == 0 (or differs from the count expected in the config), return INVALID_INPUT (no predictions for sector). Consider locking n_predicted in the config.

findings.title: Median baseline error is understated in the error formula
findings.evidence: err = beta*sig*sqrt(1/n_in + 1/n_out) treats the median baseline as a mean; the variance of a median is about pi/2 times larger. White-noise Monte Carlo (3000 draws, T14 = 1/2/4.4 h, D = 0.5/1/2 x ref): std(dep/err) = 1.035-1.056.
findings.fix: Use sqrt(1/n_in + (pi/2)/n_out), or a bootstrap, or simply let the beta/empirical calibration absorb it, and document that choice.

findings.title: comparable() compares the band fit with an any-duration fit at a different offset, so it is not a duration test at the fitted time
findings.evidence: 70441745 settings, 20 seeds: an on-time reference transit alone is RECOVERED 20/20. Adding a 3-h, 0.6x-reference feature at +150 min (inside the 175-min local window) gives AMBIGUOUS 19/20. La is at +44 min / 3.0 h (SNR 9.6-11.3) while Lb is at 0..20 min (SNR 7.6-9.6), and the delta-chi2 <= 4 test fails across different offsets.
findings.fix: Profile duration at the band fit's offset (or within +-T14/2 of it): compare Lb's chi2 with the best any-duration fit at the same offset neighbourhood. Declare this in docstring step 6.

findings.title: Docstring and protocol mismatches inside the declared procedure (stale comment; 'covered' vs 'full'; flux product)
findings.evidence: The comment on lines 185-186 still describes the removed per-event 'displaced' INCONSISTENT route (DECISIONS item 72). The protocol defines 'covered' as >= 60% of cadences within +-1.5 durations and uses it for Recovered and Insufficient; the evaluator requires 'full' coverage (>= 90% in-transit plus baselines) for every outcome. test_conformance 'partial_one' (in-transit coverage about 40%, but about 80% within +-1.5 D, so 'covered' under the protocol) expects INSUFFICIENT. Line 4 nevertheless claims to implement the written protocol rules. The protocol names QLP DET_FLUX; the configs use SAP_FLUX (justified in make_conformance_configs.py but not stated as a protocol deviation).
findings.fix: Delete or correct the stale comment. List each deliberate deviation from the protocol (full vs covered, SAP vs DET_FLUX, EXCLUDED definition) explicitly in the docstring and procedure doc as declared amendments.

findings.title: Time-system check is only t.min() > 2e6
findings.evidence: QLP ext-1 headers carry TIMEREF='SOLARSYSTEM', TIMESYS='TDB', BJDREFI=2457000 (verified on S105). None are checked, so a file with a different BJDREF (e.g. BJD-2450000, about 11234) would pass.
findings.fix: For FITS input, require BJDREFI == 2457000 (plus BJDREFF ~ 0), TIMESYS == 'TDB' and TIMEREF == 'SOLARSYSTEM', otherwise return INVALID_INPUT.

findings.title: Reporting and grid details: res['joint'] always shows the local fit; the 2-min grid quantises the min() gate; the regex accepts '106.x'
findings.evidence: res['joint'] = local_max band fit even when the outcome is INCONSISTENT (the deciding fit is global_max). The offset grid has 2-min steps, so the min() reading for 206620592 (3 sigma = 4.2 min) accepts only |o| <= 4. Regex test: '106.5' matches (no such value in the current CSVs).
findings.fix: Report the deciding fit per outcome (e.g. res['deciding_fit']). Use a 1-min grid, or state the quantisation. Tighten the regex to ^106(?:\.0+)?(?:\s|$|\().
