findings.title: Equal-length (CADENCENO) branch refuses every case because TESScut CADENCENO is always 0
findings.evidence: Scan of all 57 cached cutouts in data/lk_cache/clockcheck (S<=105): CADENCENO is all zero in every one (36 with S<99, 21 with S>=99). QLP CADENCENO runs 1157894-1168985 (S96), 1263413-1274793 (S103), 1286476-1298471 (S105). Run B (S103 affected sector, 10964 = 10964 rows), Run B2 (S96 control) and s105_aligned (only the 11652 QLP rows that sit exactly on TESScut cadences) all print 'REFUSED: equal-length lists but CADENCENO differ (no absolute anchor)' and exit 2; the +200 s copy (s105_aligned_shift200) prints the same. Equal-length matching was used for 17/21 affected-sector and 36/36 control-sector measurements in results/qlp_clock_v2/*.json. All 198 authors' clock records in conf_* used 'gap-edge (3 gaps)', so this branch was never run in validation. If S106 QLP and its cutout have equal length (the usual case so far), the tool exits 2, the evaluator returns CLOCK_UNVERIFIED, and the procedure would have to change after S106 data are seen. This also applies when MAST has already fixed the times (S96 is refused).
findings.fix: Replace the elementwise CADENCENO equality with a check that does not rely on astrocut's CADENCENO. One candidate: the earlier increments check (diff of QLP CADENCENO equals round(diff(sc)/200 s)) plus a plausibility gate requiring (QLP - sc) to match one of the two physical states within a few seconds for nearly all cadences (constant about -3 s if unfixed, or LTT(t)+c0 if fixed), refusing otherwise. This would also reject a 200-s row misalignment. The cutout's FFI_FILE column (e.g. 'tess2026164215231-s0105-2-2-0307-s_ffi') is a possible absolute anchor, but QLP carries no FFI name, and whether QLP CADENCENO numbering equals SPOC FFI numbering is unverified. So the declared >= 2 gaps refusal and the offset measurement apply to a file other than the one the record names. A record that cannot be checked against its input defeats the clock gate, and CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE line 93 says this record will be reported.

The claim is literally true. In scripts/qlp_clock_test_sector.py, the script chooses the branch at line 28 using len(tq) read from a.qlp (line 21). In the unequal-length branch, line 32 calls q.qlp_minus_sc(tic, sec). That function (qlp_clock_v2.py:35-36) looks the QLP file up again with qlp_file() (line 12), a glob over ROOT/data/qlp*/hlsp_qlp_tess_ffi_s{sec:04d}-{tic:016d}_tess_v01_llc.fits that never sees a.qlp. So in the unequal branch, the >=2-gap refusal and the QLP-minus-spacecraft offsets are computed from whatever file the glob returns, not from the file the record names. The branch choice and the measurement are not even guaranteed to use the same file. I reproduced this myself on the published script version (unpatched).

findings.title: --allow-no-clock silently skips the clock gate for QLP sectors >= 99

findings.title: Gap-edge method has no consistency or plausibility check; one misregistered gap is silently blended into corrections
findings.evidence: s105_misreg_gap2.fits: QLP lacks the last FFI before gap 2 and has one extra FFI 200 s before TESScut's first FFI after the gap; all time labels are correct. With the lookup patched, it is accepted as 'gap-edge (3 gaps)' with offsets [-1.382, -2.632, -0.052] min and corrections [4.002, 5.847, 3.875] against the true [2.672, 3.266, 3.875], a bias of +1.33 / +2.58 min. offset_range [-3.385, -0.052] is recorded but nothing acts on it. The scenario is realistic: TESScut S105 lacks 71 FFIs that QLP has, so the two FFI sets do differ. Matching all cadences by nearest time on the same file gives 11651/11651 at -3 s (the extra cadence falls in the TESScut gap and is left unmatched). A uniform +200 s label shift is also accepted as a +3.28-min clock offset with no flag; the final times come out right, but nothing tells it apart from a misregistration.
findings.fix: Require the matched offsets to agree: spread below about 5 s for the unfixed state, or residuals from LTT(t)+c0 below about 5 s for the fixed state; refuse otherwise. Better, match all cadences under each hypothesis rather than only gap edges. Nearest-time matching alone aliases for offsets above 100 s, such as a MAST-fixed product with LTT of about 2-4 min, so the hypothesis offset must be subtracted first.

The code claim is literally true. In scripts/qlp_clock_v2.py:44-50, a gap is matched only when its length agrees within 1 min (|g2-g|<1) and its start agrees within 20 min (|a2-a|*1440<20). Both edge offsets are then appended, and nothing checks that the offsets agree across edges or across gaps. scripts/qlp_clock_test_sector.py:33 accepts any 'gap-edge' result with at least 2 gaps. Line 36 interpolates dt to each event, and offset_range_over_sector_min is written at line 40 but never read anywhere in scripts/. prereg_conformance.py:127 uses only event_btjd and correction_min. I reproduced the reviewer's file directly through q.qlp_minus_sc: it is accepted with one gap's edges 3.33 min off and no flag.

Discounts:
(1) The reviewer overstates how realistic this is. On the real S105 data the 71 extra QLP FFIs all sit at the sector end (BTJD 4233.018-4233.180), not at any gap edge. The only real gap-edge mismatch on disk (TIC 258006047 S102, where TESScut has 22 extra FFIs at the start of gap 2) was correctly rejected by the gap-length tolerance (690 vs 616.67 min). Every gap-edge case that was accepted on disk has an offset spread of 0.00 s. The failure needs the same shift at both edges of one gap, and no sector on disk shows that.
(2) The uniform +200 s label shift is not a defect. A uniform shift is a clock offset, and the reviewer agrees the corrected times come out right.

Severity: major. The max(3 sigma, 30 min) gate that was adopted would survive a one-FFI shift (about 3.3 min). But the min(3 sigma, 30 min) companion reading, declared in results/CLARIFICATION_TIMING_RULE_2026-10-20.md:18, has gates of about 4.2, 6.3, 8.3 and 10.2 min for TICs 206620592, 120444365, 183374279 and 115692561. A 1.3-3.3 min bias is 30-80% of those gates. Because the start tolerance is 20 min and the length tolerance is 1 min, an equal shift of up to about 5-6 FFIs is accepted, so the bias has no check below about 20 min.

Caveat on the fix: a raw 'spread < 5 s' test would wrongly refuse a correctly MAST-fixed product, because there QLP minus spacecraft equals LTT(t)+c0, which varies by about 1.2 min over S105 (2.59 to 3.79 min). The check must test residuals after subtracting the hypothesis, as the second clause of the proposed fix says. The fix costs nothing on the real data, where the spread is 0.00 s.

votes.reason:
I reproduced the mechanism exactly. I rebuilt the misregistered file myself, and both qlp_clock_v2.qlp_minus_sc and the real qlp_clock_test_sector.py (with qlp_file patched) accept it as 'gap-edge (3 gaps)'. The corrections come out as [4.002, 5.847, 3.875] min against the true [2.672, 3.266, 3.875], matching the finding to the digit. Nothing checks that the offsets measured at different gaps agree. offset_range_over_sector_min is written to the clock record, but prereg_conformance.py:127 reads only event_btjd and correction_min.

The finding overstates two things. First, a plausibility check does exist: qlp_clock_v2.py:49 requires gap lengths to agree within 1 min and gap starts within 20 min. On real data that check rejected the only gap-edge mismatch I found. Second, the realism argument is weak: the 71 FFIs that QLP has and TESScut lacks in S105 all fall at the end of the sector, not at a gap edge. The defect is therefore narrower than the title says: there is no cross-gap offset-agreement check. It only triggers when both edges of one gap shift by the same number of cadences, in opposite directions of set difference. That pattern does not occur in any of the 4 unequal-length pairs on disk.

Severity is minor, not major. Under the adopted 30-min gate, a bias of 1.3-2.6 min (k=1) does not change the outcome. Within the 20-min tolerance the worst case is k=5, which gives up to 12.9 min on one event. That would exceed the alternative min(3 sigma, 30) reading of 6.3-8.3 min, but only with an even more contrived pattern of 3 or more cadences, applied to a single event inside a joint common-offset fit. The context that keeps it worth fixing: gap-edge is the only path that can produce an S106 clock record, and the fix is cheap. I dropped the uniform +200 s item, because the finding itself concedes the final times come out right.

findings.title: '>= 2 matched gap edges' in the docs, but the code requires >= 2 matched gaps (4 edges); refusal message is misleading
findings.evidence: Line 33 parses the gap count from 'gap-edge (N gaps)' and refuses if N < 2. The patched one-gap copy (2 edges matched) printed 'REFUSED: fewer than 2 matched gap edges'.
findings.fix: State '>= 2 matched data gaps (4 edges)' in the docstring, the procedure document and the message, or change the rule to match the wording.

findings.title: LTT is evaluated at ev - off, labelled spacecraft time but it is not (negligible)
findings.evidence: ev is the barycentric predicted time, so spacecraft time is about ev - LTT - c0, roughly 3 min earlier, not ev - off. Effect is negligible: when off changed by 3.33 min (patched shift200 run), the LTT changed by only 0.0003 min (2.5881 to 2.5878).
findings.fix: Use ev - (LTT0 + c0)/1440 with one iteration, or correct the comment and docstring.

findings.title: offset_range_over_sector_min covers only the matched gap edges in gap-edge mode
findings.evidence: Run A records [-0.05165, -0.05164], taken from the 6 gap-edge values only. In the misregistered case it was [-3.385, -0.052] and nothing acted on it.
findings.fix: Rename it, or compute it over all matched cadences and use it in the consistency check (see the gap-edge finding).

findings.title: Interpolation between gap edges and constant extrapolation past the last edge are crude for a MAST-fixed product
findings.evidence: In the simulated fixed product (s105_fixed), edge offsets span 2.28-3.75 min because they follow LTT. Corrections were +0.020 / -0.005 / +0.068 min, the largest for the event 0.58 d after the last gap edge (part of this comes from my Earth-centre LTT approximation, accurate to about 1 s). An event several days from an edge would see a larger error; this is extrapolated from dLTT/dt, not measured. Negligible against the 30-min gate.
findings.fix: Use offsets from all matched cadences instead of only gap edges.

findings.title: 'No flux is read' is literally false
findings.evidence: fits.open(memmap=False) followed by h[1].data loads the whole binary table, including SAP_FLUX in QLP and the FLUX cube in the cutout. The downloaded S106 cutout (cutout_size=3) will contain the target's pixel flux. Flux is not used or examined, but the statement is inaccurate.
findings.fix: Reword to 'flux columns are neither used nor examined', or open with memmap=True and read only the TIME/TIMECORR/CADENCENO columns.

findings.title: cut() has no holdout guard and no camera/CCD check
findings.evidence: For any sector without a cached cutout, cut() calls lk.search_tesscut and downloads into data/lk_cache/clockcheck/<tic>/ with no flag and no logged time. It takes glob f[0] when several cutouts exist and never compares the cutout's CAMERA/CCD with the QLP header (they did match for S96/S103/S105). The only thing that prevents an S106 fetch now is the order of the QLP SECTOR assert (line 20 before line 22). prereg_v2.py already has a holdout guard (DECISIONS 69); this helper does not.
findings.fix: Add an explicit --allow-download flag (or date check) for sectors >= 106 that logs the UTC time of the download, and check that the cutout's camera/CCD matches the QLP header.

findings.title: Ramps after orbit gaps give false RECOVERED, false INCONSISTENT and false EXCLUDED (with a real transit present); there is no edge policy, and locked S106 epochs fall in the affected zone
findings.location: scripts/prereg_conformance.py:130-137 (detrend/mask; no edge or segment policy), :102-105 (constant-median baseline), :141 (eligibility); docstring lines 17-22; results/CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md:84

CLI runs on real S105 QLP SAP data (product 'synthetic' plus CSV; no signal unless stated):
- 120444365, predictions at 4207.26 and 4221.34 (0.6 d after data resume after the two orbit gaps; no real transit within the 0.84-d window) gave RECOVERED: +26 min, 2.30 h, 884 ppm (1.03x reference), SNR 5.91, p=0.65.
- 183374279, 3 predictions at 4207.29, 4214.325 and 4221.36 gave INCONSISTENT: +54 min, 993 ppm, SNR 7.55, p=0.015, per-event depths 1225/469/1311.
- 183374279 with reference transits (1090 ppm, 2.84 h) injected exactly at 4206.69 and 4220.76 gave EXCLUDED. The stack at the predicted time is -1174 ± 169 ppm (per event -1490 and -845); each event's own best dip is the ramp (6986 ppm at -432 min; 5396 ppm at +182 min).

Ramp size (ramp_profile.py, residual after the evaluator's own 0.7-d biweight, first 0.2 d after data resume following an orbit gap): -8809 and -8654 ppm for 183374279 S105; -6997 and -6895 ppm for 183374279 S96; ±1000-1800 ppm for 120444365 and 115692561. The structure persists to about 1 d (for example +1132 ppm at 0.6-0.8 d).

The authors' own calibration shows the same pattern:
- 6 of their 8 false RECOVERED/INCONSISTENT nulls had an eligible event less than 0.6 d after a segment start: 6/38 near a start versus 2/62 elsewhere (Fisher one-sided p=0.033).
- The only round-2 false RECOVERED (183374279 null_0.3112) is ramp-driven. Its event at 4206.829 is 0.54 d after the 4206.29 start; that event's own best dip is 4466 ppm at SNR 20 (+146 min). The joint fit lands at exactly +30 min with p=0.0122. The document attributes the '1 in 50' false rate to noise (line 84).

S106 schedule (orbit-table times converted to BTJD):
- 120444365 epoch 562 (4249.859) is 1.78 d after the orbit-224 start. In S105, this star's first QUALITY=0 cadence came 1.24-1.43 d after the orbit start, so this epoch would sit about 0.35-0.55 d into the data. Epoch 563 (4255.007) is 0.09 d after the downlink restart.
- 183374279 epoch 246 (4250.127) is 2.05 d after the orbit start. With the S105 lag of 0.87-1.05 d, it would sit about 1.0-1.2 d into the data. The test rests on epochs 245 and 246.

S106-geometry analog (each S106 prediction mapped to the same position in S105 segments, reference transit injected): 183374279 was RECOVERED in only 1/4 eligible placements (shift ±0.2 d), against 8/11 in the authors' random-phase calibration. CLI at +0.2 d gave AMBIGUOUS: fit at +42 min, driven by event 1, whose own best dip is the ramp (2872 ppm at +183 min).

The search pipeline masks 0.3 d at segment edges (tsearch.trim_edges, scripts/tsearch.py:57-65), and the 183374279 addendum cites 'the pipeline's 0.3-d end-of-sector trim'; the evaluator has neither. Adding a 0.3-d trim in-process did not cure it (183374279 nulls were still INCONSISTENT at 0.5 and 1.0 d). A 0.6-d trim still left one false INCONSISTENT.
findings.fix: Before any S106 data are examined, declare an edge and systematics policy and calibrate it. For example: an event is ineligible if its evaluation window (tc ± (0.3 d + 3 x 2 x T14)) overlaps the first ~1.0 d after data resume following an orbit gap, or lies within 0.3 d of any gap; fewer than 2 remaining events gives INSUFFICIENT. Alternatively, use the protocol's local linear (or quadratic) baseline and a per-event ramp diagnostic. Re-run the null/injection calibration with phases stratified by distance to segment starts. Replace the '1 in 50' statement with rates measured near and away from edges, and state the S106 epochs at risk.

I could not refute the claim. Every point I could check is true, either by reading the code or by reproducing it.

(1) No edge policy. prereg_conformance.py:130-137 builds the transit mask, runs a biweight detrend with break_tolerance=0.5 and selects out-of-transit points. Nothing removes cadences near segment starts or ends. Eligibility at :141 only needs in-transit coverage of at least 0.9 and a baseline of at least 0.5xT14 on each side. The pipeline's own trim (tsearch.trim_edges, scripts/tsearch.py:57-65) is never called. The 183374279 addendum (line 24) cites "the pipeline's 0.3-d end-of-sector trim". DECISIONS.md item 8 records that gap-edge ramps produced every v1 SDE>9 candidate.

(2) Baseline. :102-105 takes a constant median baseline. The protocol (PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:42) says "local linear baseline".

(3) CLI cases. I re-ran all four of the reviewer's cases through the unchanged CLI and got the stated numbers exactly. First I confirmed the input CSVs are the real S105 QLP SAP data, with only the stated injections (max|df| = 2e-16).

(4) Ramp profile. My own measurement matches: -8809/-8654 ppm for 183374279 S105 and -6997/-6895 ppm for S96 in the first 0.2 d after an orbit gap. There is +1132 ppm at 0.6-0.8 d.

(5) Calibration. From the authors' JSONs I get 6/38 false RECOVERED/INCONSISTENT near a segment start versus 2/62 elsewhere, Fisher p=0.0325. The 0.3112 case matches the description.

(6) Locked S106 epochs. The orbit-table lags check out. Epoch 562 of 120444365 would fall about 0.35-0.54 d into the data; epoch 246 of 183374279 about 1.0-1.17 d in.

Three points need qualifying, but none refutes the claim:
(a) The '6 of 8' figure mixes in round-1 INCONSISTENT outcomes decided under a rule that has since been replaced. I re-ran the 5 near-start round-1 false nulls with the current code. Four of them become EXCLUDED or AMBIGUOUS, and one (0.3787, 0.18 d after a start) is still RECOVERED. Under the current code the comparison is 2/38 false RECOVERED near a start (0.18 d and 0.54 d) against 0/62 elsewhere. That is the same direction, but p is only about 0.14.
(b) Procedure doc line 84 states the unconditional '1 in 50' rate without splitting it by distance from an edge. It does not literally say 'noise'; line 78 is where noise is invoked.
(c) Calling the 4466-ppm dip at 0.64 d 'the ramp' is an interpretation. The unmasked residuals there are positive, so this dip is an artifact of the masked detrend near the segment start. It is still caused by the edge.

Not verified:
- The S106 exposure assumes the S105 lag repeats. I could not check this without S106 data, which the rules forbid.
- Epoch 563 sits after a downlink restart. Those first bins show only ±100-500 ppm, so the exposure there is weaker.
- I did not re-check the '1/4 placements' and trim experiments, which came from the reviewer's fastconf.py re-implementation. I checked only the +0.2 d CLI case.

Severity if real is blocker. The declared procedure can return a false RECOVERED on real null data and EXCLUDED with a real transit present. It can do so at positions the locked epochs plausibly occupy, and the remedy has to be declared before any S106 data are examined.

votes.reason:
I could not refute the finding. Every CLI result it reports came out the same when I re-ran it. The evaluator also has no edge or segment policy, which I confirmed by reading the code. And the locked S106 epochs fall where the in-sample data show a large ramp after an orbit gap.

Reproductions (12 evaluator runs, all on S105 QLP SAP with QUALITY==0, CSV input):
- Run A, 120444365 nulls at 4207.26 and 4221.34: RECOVERED. +26 min, 884 ppm, SNR 5.91, p=0.653. The finding's numbers match.
- Run B, 183374279 nulls at 4207.29, 4214.325 and 4221.36: INCONSISTENT. +54 min, 993 ppm, SNR 7.55, p=0.0152, per-event depths 1225/469/1311. The numbers match.
- Run C, 183374279 with transits injected at 4206.69 and 4220.76: EXCLUDED. Stack at the prediction is -1174 ± 169 ppm; each event's best dip is 6986 ppm at -432 min and 5396 ppm at +182 min. The numbers match.
- Ramp residuals also match: -8809/-8654 ppm (S105) and -6997/-6895 ppm (S96) for 183374279, and +1132 ppm at 0.6-0.8 d.
- The round-2 false RECOVERED (null_0.3112) matches: its event 0.54 d after a segment start has a best dip of 4466 ppm at SNR 20, and the joint fit lands at +30 min with p=0.0122.
- The orbit-table arithmetic matches: 1.774, 2.042 and 0.085 d; S105 lags of 0.871-1.049 d (183374279) and 1.241-1.429 d (120444365).

The key evidence is the raw SAP flux after the orbit-222 start. It begins at -45,500 ppm and is still -8800 to -5600 ppm at 1.0-1.2 d, which is where 183374279 epoch 246 should fall. In that region the biweight residual swings by ±2-3.6 ppt, and the pattern changes with the position of the prediction mask.

At the S106 analog geometry for 183374279:
- The three null placements (J/K/L) were all AMBIGUOUS, so there was no false positive.
- Injected transits were RECOVERED in only 1 of 3 placements (D, E, F). The authors' round-2 calibration gives 8 of 11. My control G, with the second event moved off the ramp, was RECOVERED.
- In the one RECOVERED analog (D), the event near the orbit start measured 1799 ppm for a 1090-ppm injection, and p=0.0132 sat just above the 0.01 cut.

So the risk for S106 is mainly that a real transit is scored AMBIGUOUS. That undercuts the "90% recovered" power statement for this epoch, and fixing it after the data are seen would be post hoc. On that basis I rate it a blocker.

Caveats:
1. My calibration table is 6/29 near a segment start versus 2/71 elsewhere (Fisher p=0.007), not 6/38 versus 2/62. 4. The false-alarm part (wide gates for 70441745 and 253931796) was not reproduced. I ran no nulls on those targets, so it is unverified.

It is fixed with a document edit such as the proposed per-test table. That edit must be made before any S106 data are examined, since a power statement added afterwards is post hoc. That constrains when to fix it, not how severe it is.

The reviewer's claim that these two tests are expected to come out AMBIGUOUS whatever the truth is supported. EXCLUDED is effectively out of reach by the evaluator's own rule, and AMBIGUOUS came out in 4/6 and 5/6 injections.

findings.title: Asymmetric thresholds (RECOVERED SNR>=5, INCONSISTENT SNR>=7) and the opposite50 change deviate from the written protocol but are presented as conformance
findings.evidence: The protocol's Inconsistent clause reads: 'a dip of comparable depth and duration exists within +-0.3 d ... its time differs by more than 30 min from every predicted time'. It has no SNR >= 7 and no common-offset requirement. The look-elsewhere difference between the local RECOVERED region (+-90-115 min) and the INCONSISTENT search (+-432 min) is roughly 4-8x in trials, which under Gaussian noise justifies about 0.5 sigma, not 2 sigma. The heavy tails apply equally to RECOVERED. Empirical consequences: 2/100 false RECOVERED vs 0/51 false INCONSISTENT, and only 2/6 displaced transits detected. test_conformance.py's docstring still says 'Expected outcomes are declared below BEFORE running', yet line 22 records that opposite50 was changed after calibration from INCONSISTENT (the literal protocol reading: each dip is more than 30 min from every predicted time) to AMBIGUOUS. Procedure line 61 still counts it among '15/15 ... give the declared outcome'.
findings.fix: Label SNR >= 7 and the common-offset requirement as deviations from the written rule. Set both thresholds to a common calibrated false-alarm rate, or apply the same threshold to both outcomes. Correct the test docstring and the '15/15 declared' wording, and also report opposite50 under the literal protocol reading.

votes.reason: I could not refute the core claim; it holds as written. The protocol's Inconsistent clause (PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:51-52) and the v2 registrations ((2), e.g. 120444365/PREREGISTRATION_v2.md:21) contain no SNR>=7 and no common-offset requirement. The evaluator adds both: line 187 requires Gb["snr"]>=7.0, and lines 161-165 and 182 make INCONSISTENT depend on a common-offset joint fit with chi2-consistent depths, while per-event displaced dips are information only (docstring 37-38, line 150). The docstring nevertheless says "It implements the written protocol outcome rules" (line 4), and the procedure is presented as the conformance procedure (CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE:1,12). The changes are disclosed as calibration changes (docstring 36-38, procedure:78, DECISIONS item 72), so they are not hidden. But none of these places labels them as departures from the written rule; line 78 only hints at this ("RECOVERED threshold stays at the protocol's SNR >= 5"). The test docstring (test_conformance.py:4) says expectations were declared BEFORE running, yet line 22 records that opposite50 was changed after calibration. Under the literal protocol, opposite50 is INCONSISTENT: each dip is comparable and lies 50 min from its prediction, which is beyond the 30-min gate. The evaluator returns AMBIGUOUS. Its stated reason ("no common offset -> not a coherent wrong ephemeris") is also doubtful: offsets of -50/+50 at two consecutive epochs fit a linear ephemeris with a period error exactly, and a wrong ephemeris is the case the Inconsistent clause names. The Gaussian look-elsewhere argument is correct. Rescoring the authors' own calibration outputs shows the empirical asymmetry is small: with SNR>=5, the joint route gives about 4/100 false INCONSISTENT against 2/100 false RECOVERED, and the strongest null was SNR 5.75, so a threshold of 7 overshoots. One detail is overstated. The "2/6 displaced transits detected" figure comes from one reviewer batch (stat-honesty). A second batch of 6 injections displaced by 60 min or more gave 4/6 INCONSISTENT. Taken together, about half are detected, and the misses mostly have SNR 6.4-6.8 (blocked by the threshold of 7) or a depth above 1.5x.

I could not refute it. Each factual claim in the finding matches the files. The real-data cases in validate_conformance_real.py are fixed and deterministic: three light curves, each run as transit, half-phase null and half-phase injection. DECISIONS 71 says that real injections drove at least one design change: "per-event-only matching failed real injections (1/3) -> joint fit". The diff from jointglobal to precalib rewrites the RECOVERED rule itself. The old test applied the 0.7-1.3x duration check to the single best box. The new one compares a band-duration fit against the best fit at any duration (delta-chi2 <= 4) and adds a new local offset region. The docstring credits that change to "shown by injection, see validation".

The procedure document gives 3/3, 0/3 and 3/3 under "Validation" (lines 68-71) without saying that these cases were used during development. It discloses only the round-1 to round-2 calibration change (line 78). The sentence "RECOVERED threshold stays at SNR >= 5 and was not tuned" is literally true about the number 5. As the finding says, the rest of the RECOVERED rule was changed on these cases.

findings.title: Calibration did not use the locked settings (120444365 duration; sigma_min and narrow gate)
findings.evidence: CASES uses ref_dur 2.18 h for 120444365. The locked config and dated amendment use 2.0 h, which is the BLS duration_h under the generator rule; no 2.18 appears in report.json. Duration sets the transit mask, coverage, the beta bin, the 0.7-1.3x band and the local search region. sigma_min is hard-coded to 3.0 min, giving a 9-min min() gate. The locked S106 sigma_min mean for 120444365 is 2.1 min, a 6.3-min gate. So 'min() reading recovers 31/51 (61%)' was computed with the wrong narrow gate.
findings.fix: Read the reference depth and duration from configs/conformance/*.json and sigma_min from the actual prediction files, then re-run the calibration.

votes.reason: I could not refute the finding. Its factual claims hold, from the file readings and from my reproduction. Every calibration and validation run for TIC 120444365 used ref_dur_h 2.18 h and sigma_min 3.0 min, which gives a 9-min min() gate. The locked S106 test uses 2.0 h and sigma_min 2.1 min, which gives a 6.3-min gate. One part of the claim is overstated: the narrower gate by itself does not change the 31/51 figure. When I re-applied the 6.3-min gate (8.3 min for TIC 183374279) to the authors' existing outputs, the count stayed at 31/51. The offset grid is in 2-min steps and no min-RECOVERED injection for 120444365 had |offset| = 8. The duration mismatch does matter. Re-running at the locked settings moves the fitted offsets and SNRs, and individual outcomes change in both directions. So the published 90% and 61% power and the 2% false-positive rate are unverified for the locked procedure, not shown false. The six cases I re-ran were chosen near the SNR threshold, so they show that results are sensitive to the setting. They do not estimate how much the aggregate rates would move. findings.title: 'EXCLUDED is rarely reachable' contradicts the document's own numbers; give the precision required
findings.evidence: Nulls came out EXCLUDED 9/51 (18%) in round 2 and 11/49 (22%) in round 1, or 13/49 (27%) under the final rule. For a null, P(EXCLUDED) = Phi(0.3S - 3). Even odds need S = 10; 90% needs S = 14.3, i.e. a stacked error <= 0.07x the reference. This matches observation (1.6/4.5/3.2 predicted vs 1/5/3 observed). For S106: 253931796 (S about 32-40) is near-certain EXCLUDED for a null; 70441745 (S about 10) about 49%; 115692561 and 122522485 about 2-4%. For a true reference-depth transit, Phi(-0.7S - 3) is about 0.

votes.reason: I could not refute it. Everything the finding states either checks out exactly or comes out close. The EXCLUDED rule in the code is depth + 3*err < 0.3*ref, measured at offset 0 with the reference duration. For a null with Gaussian depth errors that gives P(EXCLUDED) ~ Phi(0.3S - 3), where S = ref / stacked error. The probabilities this formula predicts match the authors' own calibration runs. Those runs put null EXCLUDED rates at 18% (round 2), 22% (round 1) and 27% (round 1 under the final rule). Saying "EXCLUDED is rarely reachable" at those numbers is an overstatement. For the S106 tests the reachability also depends heavily on the target. In-sample (S<=105) noise says a null on TIC 253931796 comes out EXCLUDED almost certainly, so the document's blanket "a non-transiting signal will usually come out AMBIGUOUS, not EXCLUDED" is wrong for that test. Several of the finding's per-target numbers are optimistic, so the fix should quote ranges, not single values: about 49% for 70441745 (my estimate: 16-51%) and 2-4% for 115692561 and 122522485 (mine: 3-6%). The problem is limited to the document's power statement. The evaluator's logic and outcomes are unaffected, so I rate it minor, not major.

findings.title: The configs depart from the public protocol's light-curve column and reference values, and nothing says so
findings.evidence: PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:37-39 says the test uses 'the first public light curve of the test sector (SPOC PDCSAP if 2-min data exist, otherwise QLP DET_FLUX; and, as a cross-check, a TESScut fixed-aperture extraction)'. Lines 42-43 say 'Reference depth and duration are the values in each PREREGISTRATION file (... TIC 120444365: 750 ppm, 2.0 h; TIC 183374279: 970 ppm, 2.9 h ...)'. None of the 7 TICs is in catalogs/tesscurl_sector_106_lc.sh, so by the protocol the column is QLP DET_FLUX. All 7 configs lock SAP_FLUX, and set 855 ppm/2.0 h (120444365) and 1090 ppm/2.84 h (183374279). The 120444365 amendment justifies itself only by saying 'this registration predates the template line'; it never mentions the protocol's 750 ppm. The document (line 40) gives a reason for using SAP but never says it overrides the protocol. Nothing addresses the protocol's TESScut cross-check. This conflict was flagged in REVIEW_timing_rule.md:369 ('State the hierarchy'), and REVIEW_S106_test_procedure.md:9 shows that switching between SAP_FLUX and DET_FLUX turned RECOVERED into INCONSISTENT on an earlier sector.
findings.fix: Before publishing, add a dated precedence statement to the document and to each amendment. It should list the protocol's column (DET_FLUX) and its values (750/2.0, 970/2.9) next to the locked ones, give the reason for each override, and say whether the protocol's TESScut cross-check is dropped. Commit to reporting the outcome under the protocol's column and values as a secondary reading, so the choice of column cannot decide the result.

votes.reason:
I could not refute it. Reading the files confirms every clause. The protocol fixes the light curve as SPOC PDCSAP when 2-min data exist, otherwise QLP DET_FLUX, with a TESScut cross-check. It also lists reference values: 750 ppm / 2.0 h for TIC 120444365 and 970 ppm / 2.9 h for TIC 183374279. None of the 7 TICs has S106 2-min data, so the protocol's column is DET_FLUX, which is also the frozen evaluator's QLP default. All 7 locked configs use SAP_FLUX, with 855/2.0 and 1090/2.84. The conformance document, its script docstring, the config generator, the configs, the amendments and the timing clarification never mention DET_FLUX, PDCSAP, 750 ppm or 970 ppm, and none says it overrides the protocol.

It is worse than written in one way. The only reason the document gives (line 40: SAP is "the raw-SAP basis of every frozen ephemeris and reference depth") is wrong about the protocol's own values. Both are DET_FLUX/BLS depths, not raw-SAP: 970 matches bls_refine 968.6 (SAP gives 1092), and 750 matches v1's "743 ppm (QLP, masked detrend)" (SAP gives 855.3). For TIC 120444365, 750/2.0 was the only reference value stated publicly before the amendment. The amendment replaces it with 855, which is 14% higher and moves both the 0.5-1.5x RECOVERED band and the 0.3x EXCLUDED threshold, and it never names 750.

Scope limits, so the finding is not overstated:
(a) The protocol table names only 120444365 and 183374279 of the 7 S106 objects. The other 5 come under the protocol only through their timing addenda ("The governing rule is the public protocol's"). Their reference values match their own frozen registration lines, which the protocol defers to. So the column point covers all 7, but the reference-value point covers only 2.
(b) For 183374279, 1090/2.84 and SAP_FLUX come from the object's own frozen 2026-10-19 addendum section 2. The protocol both defers to "the values in each PREREGISTRATION file" and lists 970/2.9 in brackets, so it contradicts itself. The document's table entry "frozen registration line and addendum" cites a source but does not state which rule wins.
(c) Document lines 54-57 withdraw a TESScut fallback for 183374279. That is a different thing from the protocol's TESScut cross-check, which nothing addresses for any of the 7.

Severity: blocker, as a must-fix before publication. The evaluator code is not at fault, and the choices were locked before any S106 data were examined. But this document's only job is to be the published declaration. Published as is, it records a false statement about the protocol's values and a change to them it never discloses. Fixing it afterwards would be a post hoc amendment. The fix is one dated paragraph saying which rule takes precedence (plus a secondary reading under DET_FLUX with 750/2.0 and 970/2.9). No evaluator runs were needed. This was a documentary check, and no S106 photometry was opened.

votes.reason:
I could not refute it. Every part of the finding checks out against the files. The public protocol names QLP DET_FLUX for these targets (none of the 7 TICs has 2-min S106 data) and gives reference values of 750 ppm / 2.0 h for 120444365 and 970 ppm / 2.9 h for 183374279. All 7 configs lock SAP_FLUX, with 855/2.0 and 1090/2.84. Neither the conformance document, the amendments, the config generator nor DECISIONS 71-73 says that the protocol is being overridden, states which source takes precedence, or mentions the protocol's TESScut cross-check. A prior review (REVIEW_timing_rule.md:369) asked for exactly this ("State the hierarchy"), and it was not done. This is the opposite of the timing rule, where the authors wrote down explicitly that the protocol governs.

I also re-ran the conformance evaluator on in-sample data, swapping the flux column and the reference values (8 runs). The primary max() outcome was RECOVERED in every combination on all 3 light curves, and switching 855 to 750 or 1090 to 970 changed nothing. So the claim that the column choice can decide the main conformance result is not reproduced. The column choice does change things the document commits to report, though:
- For TIC 120444365 S96 under the min() reading, SAP_FLUX gives AMBIGUOUS (offset +16 min) and DET_FLUX gives RECOVERED (offset 0 min).
- For S105 the offset moves from +10 to +12 min.
- This affects the document's statement that the real transits sit +10 to +18 min from the ephemeris.
- The frozen evaluator's flip on an earlier sector (REVIEW_S106_test_procedure.md:9) is a separate, already documented case.

My severity is major, not blocker. The deviation is real and undisclosed, and the disclosure has to be added before any S106 data are examined, because it cannot credibly be added afterwards. But the primary max() outcome did not depend on the column in any in-sample case I tested.

findings.title: TIC 70441745 cannot get a clock record, so the declared procedure refuses to score it
findings.evidence: results/qlp_clock_v2/ holds c0 files for the other 6 configured TICs but not for 70441745. Running the clock script with the locked config and a dummy --qlp path stopped at line 18 with 'FileNotFoundError: ... results/qlp_clock_v2/70441745.json'. This happens before any FITS file is opened. Without a clock record, the evaluator returns CLOCK_UNVERIFIED for every QLP sector from 99 on. The c0 files are not listed as locked inputs anywhere in the document. 5 of the 6 existing files have c0_source = None. In-sample QLP control sectors S68 and S96 for 70441745 are on disk.
findings.fix: Generate results/qlp_clock_v2/70441745.json now from the in-sample control sectors (qlp_clock_v2.py; S68/S96), before publishing. List every per-TIC c0 file with its SHA-256 in the document as a locked input.

(1) /Users/fernando/Desktop/NASA/results/qlp_clock_v2/ has c0 JSONs for all six other configured TICs (115692561, 120444365, 122522485, 183374279, 206620592, 253931796) and none for 70441745. (2) /Users/fernando/Desktop/NASA/scripts/qlp_clock_test_sector.py:18 opens results/qlp_clock_v2/{tic}.json with no fallback, before the QLP FITS is opened at line 19. I reproduced the FileNotFoundError. (3) /Users/fernando/Desktop/NASA/scripts/prereg_conformance.py:123-124 returns "CLOCK_UNVERIFIED (no clock record supplied; scoring refused)" for a QLP sector >= 99 when --clock is not given. The only bypass is --allow-no-clock, and its help text at line 110 limits it to synthetic tests or sectors < 99, so using it on S106 would itself be a deviation. (4) The code table in /Users/fernando/Desktop/NASA/results/CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md (lines 14-22) hashes only scripts. No per-TIC c0 JSON is listed as a locked input, and this is true for all 7 configured tests, not only 70441745. (5) The c0_source key is missing in 5 of the 6 files. All six have non-empty control lists, though, so the missing key is an older file format (183374279, regenerated at 22:13, has it), not a sign that the fallback value was used. (6) QLP S28, S68 and S96 for 70441745 are on disk in data/qlp/.

Root cause I found: the c0 files were written by scripts/qlp_clock_v2.py, and the six existing ones date from freezes run with prereg_v2.py --clock (prereg_v2.py:82 reads them). The 70441745 freeze had no in-sample QLP sector >= 99: its ephemeris rows are only [(68, 'QLP SAP')]. So no c0 file was ever made for it, and the test-sector script assumes one exists.

One wording point: "cannot get a clock record" is too strong. The declared, hashed helper (qlp_clock_v2.py 70441745) would build the file from in-sample control sectors only. For this TIC it would pick S96 and S68 (lines 57-63), skip its only ephemeris row (S68 < 99), and so read nothing from S106. As things stand, though, the procedure would crash or refuse for this test unless someone runs that extra step, which is not declared.

Severity: major, not blocker. The missing input gives no room to steer the outcome. All six existing c0 values are +0.0320 to +0.0328 min (about 2 s), the module has a hardcoded +0.033 min fallback (qlp_clock_v2.py:63), and the timing gate is at least 30 min. It must be fixed before publishing so the procedure is complete, but it cannot move an outcome. The proposed fix (generate the file now from S68/S96, then list every c0 JSON with its SHA-256) is sensible.

(c) The c0 values in the existing records span 0.0320-0.0330 min (about 2 s), against timing gates of at least 30 min. findings.title: The amendment's T14 rule is misleading, and the T14 values are set inconsistently across objects
findings.location: results/vet_allsky/120444365/PREREGISTRATION_v2.md:32; results/vet_allsky/70441745/PREREGISTRATION_v2.md:28; scripts/make_conformance_configs.py:4,15; scripts/prereg_v2.py:131; CONFORMANCE doc table line 44-46
findings.evidence: No report.json contains shape_mcmc.T14_h; the keys are only names, median, lo, hi and acc. So the 'shape-fit T14 if available' branch never runs, and T14 is always the BLS grid duration. Yet a T14 can be computed from the shape_mcmc medians (rprs, ars, b) for every object: 183374279 gives 2.84 h, exactly its locked value; 120444365 gives 2.18 h (locked 2.0); 70441745 gives 1.97 h (locked 1.5). That makes 70441745's shape T14 1.31 times its locked reference, just outside the 0.7-1.3 duration band. The authors' own validation used 2.18 h for 120444365 (validate_conformance_real.py:9). The referee had computed about 2.18 h from the shape fit (REVIEW_S106_test_procedure.md:41). So 'if available' wrongly implies no shape T14 existed, and 183374279 follows a different rule from the other two, with no disclosure.
findings.fix: Rewrite both amendments and the document. Say that the shape-fit key is absent, so BLS grid durations are used. Give the shape-implied T14s (2.18 h and 1.97 h) and explain why 183374279 uses the shape value. Either apply one rule to all objects or justify the exception, before any S106 data are seen.

votes.reason:
I re-read the cited code and data and every factual claim checks out. (1) No report.json has shape_mcmc.T14_h. In all 7 S106 test objects shape_mcmc holds only names, median, lo, hi and acc, and grepping every results/vet_allsky/*/report.json for "T14_h" finds nothing. findings.title: INCONSISTENT is narrower than the protocol's clause, and the document does not call this a deviation
findings.location: scripts/test_conformance.py:22; scripts/prereg_conformance.py:187; PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:51-52; CONFORMANCE doc lines 35, 61, 78
findings.evidence: The protocol defines INCONSISTENT as a comparable dip within +-0.3 d whose 'time differs by more than 30 min from every predicted time'. The conformance evaluator instead needs one common offset across all transits and a joint SNR of at least 7. In the synthetic 'opposite50' case, with dips at -50 and +50 min and per-event SNR of about 65, the result is AMBIGUOUS, while the literal clause gives INCONSISTENT. The test file's reason, 'no common offset -> not a coherent wrong ephemeris', does not hold for a period error, which shifts timings in proportion to epoch. The document lists the change but presents the procedure as implementing the protocol rules.
findings.fix: Declare this as a dated deviation from the protocol's INCONSISTENT clause. Explain that the common-offset model cannot represent a period error and that such cases will come out AMBIGUOUS. Consider reporting the per-event displaced dips next to the outcome.

votes.reason:
I could not refute the finding. Its claims hold when checked against the code, the protocol and the authors' own outputs.

(1) The INCONSISTENT rule is narrower than the protocol's. The protocol (PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:51-52) asks only for "a dip of comparable depth and duration" within +-0.3 d whose time is more than 30 min from every predicted time. The evaluator (prereg_conformance.py:187; docstring 22, 29, 36-38) instead needs one best joint fit across all transits at a single common offset. That fit must be VALID (per-event depths consistent at chi2 p>=0.01, >=2 events positive), be "comparable" (SNR>=5, depth 0.5-1.5x, and the duration-consistency check that the best in-band-duration fit's chi2 is within 4 of the best fit at any duration), reach joint SNR>=7, and lie more than max(gate,30) min from the prediction.

(2) In opposite50 the literal clause is met but the evaluator says AMBIGUOUS. The authors' conf_test/opposite50.json has per-event best boxes at -50 min (SNR 64.5) and +50 min (SNR 65.2), both 2.0 h deep, depth about 1.18x reference, and both flagged displaced=True. The output is AMBIGUOUS/AMBIGUOUS. The only joint fit is at offset +2 min, duration 2.6 h, SNR 59.9. It fails the duration check (59.9^2 is not >= 69.3^2-4).

(3) The test file's reason (test_conformance.py:22, "no common offset -> not a coherent wrong ephemeris") is false even for its own case. Two epochs always fit a linear ephemeris: P' = P + 100 min and T0' = T0 - 150 min give -50 + 1*100 = +50, reproducing both dips. The common-offset model represents only a T0 error.

(4) Nothing calls this a deviation. Searching CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md and the docstring finds no "deviation". prereg_conformance.py:4 says "It implements the written protocol outcome rules", and doc line 24 makes that docstring the authoritative procedure.

One correction to the proposed fix. It says such cases "will come out AMBIGUOUS". My runs show some come out EXCLUDED instead. A real reference-depth signal whose offset drifts by 60 min between transits (+200/+260 min) fails the duration check. The precedence then falls through to EXCLUDED, because nothing is in the box at the predicted times. That contradicts the protocol's own gloss "(ephemeris wrong, signal real)". Drifts of 10 and 30 min still give INCONSISTENT.

Severity is major rather than blocker for one reason: the change and its calibration rationale are disclosed in doc lines 35, 61 and 78 and DECISIONS item 72. What is missing is labelling it a deviation, and the authoritative docstring misstates conformance.

Side note: the comment at prereg_conformance.py:185-186 still mentions the removed per-event route ("or >= 2 events each show their own comparable dip").

votes.reason:
I could not refute the finding. Its core claims check out by direct reading and by reproduction. (1) The protocol defines INCONSISTENT per dip: "a dip of comparable depth and duration exists within ±0.3 d ... but its time differs by more than 30 min from every predicted time". The evaluator instead requires one common-offset joint fit with joint SNR >= 7, and the protocol states no SNR threshold for INCONSISTENT. (2) I reran opposite50 and it returns AMBIGUOUS. Both events have comparable displaced dips at -50 and +50 min with SNR about 65, and the evaluator's own per-event 'displaced' flag is True for both. (3) The authors first expected INCONSISTENT for this case and changed the expectation after calibration, so they read the clause the same way before narrowing it. (4) The document discloses the change (line 78) but never labels it a deviation or amendment, although it uses 'dated amendment' for two other changes. The docstring also says the evaluator 'implements the written protocol outcome rules'.

Two parts of the finding need qualifying. First, 'the common-offset model cannot represent a period error' is too broad. My drift run (offsets +60/+80/+100) returned INCONSISTENT, because the joint box widened to 2.3 h and absorbed the ±20-min spread. The blind spot is period errors whose offsets cross zero or spread wider than the box can absorb, not period errors in general. Second, I rate the severity minor rather than major: the change is disclosed rather than hidden, it only moves cases between two non-RECOVERED labels, per-event best boxes and displaced flags are already written to the output JSON, and the document is still awaiting review before publication. The fix is a dated deviation paragraph that also notes the protocol's own tension (stacked timing for Recovered, per-dip wording for Inconsistent) and limits the period-error statement as above.

- PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:51-52 says INCONSISTENT means "a dip of comparable depth and duration exists within $\pm 0.3$ d of the predictions but its time differs by more than 30 min from every predicted time"; no SNR is given for it. The three PREREGISTRATION_v2.md files (120444365:21, 70441745:17, 183374279:18) say "a comparable dip exists but its times differ by > 30 min from every prediction".
- scripts/prereg_conformance.py:187 reads `if comparable(Ga, Gb) and Gb["snr"] >= 7.0 and abs(Gb["offset_min"]) > max(gate, 30.0): return "INCONSISTENT"`, where Ga/Gb is the common-offset joint fit. The comment at lines 185-186 still says "or >= 2 events each show their own comparable dip that far away", but the code no longer does this (DECISIONS.md:72 records that the per-event route was removed). Line 150 computes per-event 'displaced' flags for information only (docstring lines 36-38). Docstring line 4: "It implements the written protocol outcome rules".
- test_conformance.py:22 has opposite50 expected AMBIGUOUS, commented "changed 2026-10-20 after calibration: no common offset -> not a coherent wrong ephemeris".
- CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md: line 35 gives the narrowed INCONSISTENT definition, line 61 says "opposite ±50-min offsets → AMBIGUOUS", and line 78 discloses both changes. The word 'deviation' appears nowhere in the document, while 'dated amendment' is used at lines 45, 46 and 54 for other changes.
- shasum: prereg_conformance.py is 0520ea58...6d3a and test_conformance.py is b54dc38c...9e53, both matching the hashes declared in the document (lines 17 and 21).

Reproduction (my own script, wf_review/skeptic-inconsistent/repro.py, same construction as the test file, seed 99106, 3 evaluator runs):
- opposite50: outcome AMBIGUOUS (min-gate also AMBIGUOUS). Event 1 best box: offset -50 min, 2.0 h, 1178 ppm, SNR 64.5, displaced=True. Event 2: offset +50 min, 2.0 h, 1190 ppm, SNR 65.2, displaced=True. The joint fit lands at offset +2 min, duration 3.7 h, SNR 69 (band-limited: 2.6 h, SNR 60), so it is neither displaced nor comparable. Under the literal per-dip clause this case is INCONSISTENT: depth 1.18-1.19 times the 1000 ppm reference, duration equal to the reference, each dip 50 min from every prediction.
- drift60_100 (offsets +60/+80/+100 over 3 events, a period error with a large common part): outcome INCONSISTENT, joint offset +84 min, 2.3 h, SNR 85. This contradicts the claim that the common-offset model can never represent a period error.
- linear3 (offsets -50/0/+50): outcome AMBIGUOUS. The joint fit absorbs the spread into a 3.7-h box at offset +2 min, and no band-duration fit is valid locally. The middle event is not displaced, so this case does not cleanly test the 'every predicted time' wording; it only supports the point about zero-mean drift.

findings.title: 183374279's reference values are labelled 'frozen' but come from a post-freeze addendum
findings.evidence: The line containing 1090 ppm and 2.84 h is in 'ADDENDUM 2026-10-19 (after the round-2 referee review)' (PREREGISTRATION_v2.md:23-25), appended after the 11:44:14 UTC freeze. 2.84 h is the shape-implied T14, not the generator's BLS value of 2.6 h.
findings.fix: Label the source as 'dated addendum 2026-10-19 (post-freeze, pre-S106), shape-fit T14'.

findings.title: The claim that every frozen ephemeris rests on raw SAP flux is inaccurate
findings.evidence: SPOC 2-min sectors enter the ephemeris through lightkurve's default flux (lc.flux, which is PDCSAP; line 76). Affected fits: 206620592 (S28, S68), 122522485 (S3, S4, S30), 115692561 (S2) and 120444365 (S29).
findings.fix: Reword: the reference depths are QLP raw-SAP; the ephemerides combine QLP SAP with SPOC 2-min sectors where those exist.

findings.title: The clock gate can be bypassed without trace, and CSV input skips validation
findings.evidence: --allow-no-clock skips the gate, and its use is not written to the output. With a .csv light curve, the header sector/TIC check and the QUALITY filter are skipped, because sector and TIC are copied from the config. The document says scoring is 'refused' without a clock record and that inputs are validated.
findings.fix: Record allow_no_clock and the input type in the output. State that test runs must use the FITS file plus a clock record.

findings.title: The document does not say the clock record downloads S106 pixel data
findings.evidence: q.cut() downloads a 3x3 TESScut cutout of the test sector (cutout_size=3) into data/lk_cache/clockcheck/. The script reads only TIME, TIMECORR and CADENCENO from it. The ERRATUM records an earlier S106 cutout download as a disclosure event, but the document does not mention this step.
findings.fix: State that scoring downloads a test-sector cutout for its timing columns only, and log the download time in the clock record.

findings.title: The validation section overstates or leaves out a few details
findings.evidence: '15/15' counts two soft expectations: red_noise_signal min() = ANY, and red_noise_none = NOT_RECOVERED (it returned AMBIGUOUS). In round 1, 1 injection came out INCONSISTENT (my tally of conf_calib_*), which the document omits. Round 2 is called an 'independent re-check' but is the same authors re-running with fresh seeds. The INSUFFICIENT counts (22 and 18) are not given.
findings.fix: Note the soft expectations, report the round-1 injection INCONSISTENT and the INSUFFICIENT counts, and call round 2 a fresh-sample re-run.

findings.title: The software environment is not pinned
findings.evidence: Outcomes depend on wotan's biweight filter and on numpy/scipy. The venv has wotan 2.0, numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1, pandas 2.3.3, astropy 8.0.2 and lightkurve 2.6.0. The document records none of these.
findings.fix: Publish a lock file (pip freeze) with its hash in the document.

findings.title: The configs contain absolute local paths
findings.evidence: Each pred_csv is '/Users/fernando/Desktop/NASA/results/...'. The evaluator opens it directly (line 112), so a third party has to edit the locked config, which changes its hash.
findings.fix: Store repository-relative paths, resolved against a --root argument, before the configs are hashed and published.

findings.title: A stale comment in the authoritative evaluator file contradicts the final logic
findings.evidence: The comment says INCONSISTENT also fires if '>= 2 events each show their own comparable dip that far away'. That route was removed (line 187 and docstring line 37-38).
findings.fix: Delete the comment; this changes the published SHA, so do it before publishing.

findings.title: The superseded TIC 120444365 v1 S106 prediction is not mentioned
findings.evidence: The v1 file (CSV 64b5b026, own rules: depth 0.6-1.5x, 60-min cap, 743 ppm/2.0 h) is in the public preprint (Zenodo 23462433) and lists the same 6 S106 epochs, about 1.6-2.2 min earlier than v2. The document says nothing about whether it will be scored or reported.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: v1 is superseded by v2 and will (or will not) be reported, and under which rules.

findings.title: Precedence and the min() reading differ from earlier commitments without comment
findings.evidence: The frozen evaluator checks EXCLUDED before INCONSISTENT; the conformance evaluator does the reverse. The CLARIFICATION promises an 'individual-event assessment under min(3 sigma, 30 min)'. The conformance min() reading is a joint common-offset fit against the min gate; per-event match_min is only recorded for information.
findings.fix: Note the change in precedence, and state which min() quantity (joint, or per-event match_min) satisfies the CLARIFICATION's commitment.

critic.summary:
I was a completeness critic. The findings list I was given was cut off after the protocol dimension, so I judged coverage from the six summaries I could partly see and from the other reviewers' scratch directories. Grepped: skeptic-timing-para, skeptic_t14, skeptic-inj-ideal, skeptic-inject-inconsistent, skeptic_clock_record, skeptic_depthgate, skeptic-protocol-column, skeptic-power-lowsnr, adversarial/, clock/, code-correctness/, faithfulness/.

Five things were missing from the reviews:
- the public protocol's own per-object prediction sigmas, which no one cross-checked against the frozen CSVs;
- the procedure document's "Observed timing" claim, which no one checked against the registration's per-sector O-C or against an independent timing fit;
- whether the evaluator enforces the declared product (QLP SAP), and whether any rule says which release counts;
- whether the software environment is pinned;
- the time frame in which the real-data validation injects its signals.

I did the three most important checks myself. I used 2 conformance-evaluator runs (in-sample S69: one on QLP, one on TESS-SPOC). Everything else was read-only or my own numpy/wotan code on in-sample S69/S96. I opened no S106 data and modified nothing in the NASA tree. All outputs are in wf_review/completeness/ (prod/, timing/, zipx/).

Results:
1. **Protocol sigma for TIC 120444365.** The public protocol (the Zenodo v1 deposit the addenda call governing, unchanged through v1.3) gives σ 4.7 min, the v1 value. The locked v2 CSV gives 2.1 min. That puts the reported min() gate at 14.1 min under the protocol's own text and 6.3 min under the config, and the in-sample S105 transit changes outcome between the two.
2. **"Observed timing" claim.** The document says the real transits sit +10 to +18 min from the ephemeris.
   - The +18 (S96) contradicts the registration's own S96 O-C of +0.2 ± 1.8 min. My fixed-shape fit at 2.18 h gives 0.0 ± 1.5 min.
   - On the same S96 light curve, the evaluator's timing scatter for correctly timed injections is rms 8.3 min.
   - The claim treats estimator- and duration-dependent scatter as an ephemeris error.
3. **Product not enforced.** The evaluator accepts any FITS file whose SECTOR, TICID and SAP_FLUX column match. With an identical "QLP SAP_FLUX" config on in-sample S69, the QLP file gives AMBIGUOUS and the TESS-SPOC file gives RECOVERED. No rule says which product or release counts.
4. **Environment not pinned (minor).** No library versions are recorded anywhere; the bundles' requirements file is empty.
5. **Injection frame (minor).** Validation injections go in before the clock correction is applied.

These checks came out clean:
- All 7 prediction-CSV hashes match across config, local file and public git HEAD.
- Each S106 row selection is correct.
- The frozen evaluator (630815cc) is in all three Zenodo bundles.
- The public review copies differ from the local ones only by redactions.
checks_done: Read scripts/prereg_conformance.py in full (SHA-256 0520ea5858308b96..., matches CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md:17) and the procedure document in full.

Coverage audit: the input list was truncated after the protocol dimension. I listed and grepped the other reviewers' dirs under wf_review/. 253931796, 122522485, 115692561 and 206620592 were covered (skeptic-power-lowsnr, skeptic-depthgate, skeptic-excluded). Foreign clock records were covered (skeptic_clock_record/foreign*). 183374279 injection timing was covered (skeptic-inj-ideal, skeptic-inject-inconsistent). No reviewer dir mentions public_release, Zenodo bundle contents, the protocol's per-object sigmas, or product identity (ORIGIN).

Prediction-file integrity, all 7 configs: pred_sha256 in the config = sha of the local CSV = sha of public_release HEAD:preregistration/TIC*/predicted_transits_2026_2027_v2.csv = the SHA in each PREREGISTRATION_v2.md. All agree, and each file has exactly one git version. Clean.

S106 row selection per config, using the evaluator's own filter (prereg_conformance.py:119): 115692561 has 32 rows, 120444365 6, 122522485 12 (of 36; retrodictions and S107/S108 rows correctly excluded), 183374279 3, 206620592 26, 253931796 3, 70441745 2. Statuses are uniform, spacings are single-period, and no planets are mixed. Clean.

Frozen evaluator public anchoring: prereg_test.py was never committed to the GitHub public_release (git log is empty). It is in all three Zenodo bundles (zenodo_upload/preregistration_bundle_v1.1/v1.2/v1.3.zip; sha 630815cc1400). Clean, consistent with DECISIONS item 67.
The 'reviews_2026-10-20/' directory cited in the docstring exists only as public_release/reviews_2026-10-20/. diff against results/ copies shows redactions of a withheld TIC only.

Protocol versions: extracted PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex from the v1.1, v1.2 and v1.3 zips and diffed them. The v1.3 zip is byte-identical to the local tex. Line 35 (σ 4.7 min for 120444365) is the same in v1 (DOI 23462442) and v1.3. Cross-checked the other first-entry sigmas: 183374279 σ 2.7 = v2 CSV; 80387959 σ 3.5 = v2 CSV (its v1 CSV had 6.3). So the stale sigma is specific to 120444365.

Traced the 4.7: results/vet_allsky/120444365/PREREGISTRATION.md:8 (v1, epoch 559, σ 4.7, 21:54 UTC). The v2 CSV and v2_utcfix give σ 2.1 (21:55 TDB-scale, 21:51 geocentric). The protocol pairs the v2 geocentric UTC with the v1 sigma. Its table row at tex:27 gives the v2 T0 ± 2.1 min, so the protocol contradicts itself.

min() flip without an evaluator run: in conf_real/120444365_S105_transit.json and faithfulness/locked/120444365_S105_transit_locked.json, local_min band_duration is at offset +10.0 min, SNR 7.11 / 6.29, dep/ref 1.02 / 1.00, so it is comparable. The local window (l.181) is the same for both readings, so only l.184 |o| <= gate decides: 10 <= 14.1 passes, 10 <= 6.3 (or the calibration's 9.0) fails.
Read results/vet_allsky/120444365/PREREGISTRATION_v2.md:7 per-sector O-C: S69 -7.4 ± 4.2, S96 +0.2 ± 1.8, S105 +8.0 ± 5.4 min (QLP SAP).

Independent fixed-shape timing (wf_review/completeness/timing/indep.py, output indep.out). Same preprocessing as the evaluator, then a trapezoid with ingress 4 min, a common offset, per-event depth and baseline, and white-noise Δχ². Results:
- S96 at 2.18 h: 0.0 [-1.5, +1.5] min; Δχ²(+16) = 13.66.
- S96 at 2.0 h: bimodal, best +40.5, interval [-2, +42], Δχ²(0) = 1.15.
- S69 at 2.18 h: -7.5 [-13.5, +31.0].
- S69 at 2.0 h: -2.0 [-5.0, +1.5].
Caveat: my coverage test has no baseline requirement, so S96 used 5 events against the evaluator's 4.

Authors' calibration injections (conf_calib_[0-9] + conf_calib2_[0-9]; the unsuffixed conf_calib/ was excluded and not characterised, its JSONs differ byte-wise). Local band offsets for correctly timed injections:
- 120444365 S96 (n=40): median 0.0, rms 8.3 min, 28% beyond 6.3 min.
- 120444365 S105 (n=40): median 0.0, mean -2.8, rms 11.9, 33% beyond 6.3.
- 183374279 S105 (n=20): median +16, mean +19.9, rms 38.6, 25% beyond 30 min (1 INCONSISTENT). Context only; this is skeptic-inj-ideal's territory.

Product-identity attack (2 evaluator runs). I made an in-sample S69 config for 120444365 (product QLP, SAP_FLUX, locked 855 ppm / 2.0 h, σ 2.1, back-projected from final_ephemeris_v2.json; prod/mk.py). I ran it on data/qlp_allsky/hlsp_qlp_tess_ffi_s0069-...llc.fits (ORIGIN MIT/QLP) and on the TESS-SPOC HLSP s0069 lc.fits (ORIGIN NASA/Ames, PROCVER spoc-5.0.103). The evaluator accepted both without warning. Outputs: prod/s69_qlp.json, prod/s69_tessspoc.json.

Release/version rule search: grep for v01|reprocess|re-releas|first public|ORIGIN|TESS-SPOC|tglc in the procedure doc, configs, evaluator and clarification found nothing. PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:39 reads 'first public light curve of the test sector'.

Environment check:
- requirements_venv.txt is 0 bytes (sha e3b0c442...) in all three Zenodo bundles.
- git ls-tree on public_release HEAD shows no requirements or lock file.
- Installed versions: numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1, wotan 2.0 (dist-info), astropy 8.0.2, pandas 2.3.3, numba 0.68.0.
- The evaluator output JSON records no package versions.

Read validate_conformance_real.py in full (injection at l.28 on raw t) against prereg_conformance.py:127-128, which adds the clock correction. conf_real S105 clock records give corrections of +1.6 to +4.4 min.

Not done:
- S105 fixed-shape timing (it needs a decision on the clock frame the ephemeris fitter used).
- No S106 metadata or photometry was queried.
- The library-version sensitivity of outcomes was not tested.
Run budget: 2 of 12 conformance runs.

findings.title: The public protocol gives the v1 sigma (4.7 min) for TIC 120444365, not the frozen v2 sigma (2.1 min). The reported min() reading therefore has two possible gates (14.1 vs 6.3 min), and an in-sample result changes between them.
findings.evidence:
The protocol contradicts itself:
- tex:35 says 'TIC 120444365 epoch 559 at 2026-07-12 21:51 UTC (σ 4.7 min), then every 5.148171 d'.
- tex:27 says 'v2: T0 BTJD 4218.97007 ± 2.1 min'.

Where the 4.7 comes from:
- The v1 registration (PREREGISTRATION.md:8) has epoch 559 at 21:54, σ 4.7.
- The v2 CSV and v2_utcfix give σ 2.1, at 21:55 TDB-scale and 21:51 geocentric.
- So the protocol pairs the v2 geocentric UTC with the v1 sigma.

This line is the same in the v1.1 zip (the Zenodo 23462442 deposit that the timing addenda call 'the governing rule') and in v1.3. I extracted both to wf_review/completeness/zipx/.

The problem is specific to this object. The other first-entry sigmas match their v2 CSVs:
- 183374279: σ 2.7.
- 80387959: σ 3.5 (its v1 CSV had 6.3).

No declared document mentions the mismatch. I grepped the reviews, the clarification, the procedure doc and DECISIONS for '4.7': no hits.

Consequence for the min() reading, which the doc commits to reporting for every test:
- With the protocol's σ, the gate is min(3σ, 30) = 14.1 min. With the config's σ it is 6.3 min.
- In-sample S105, conf_real/120444365_S105_transit.json and faithfulness/locked/..._locked.json both have local_min band fit at +10.0 min, SNR 7.11 / 6.29, dep/ref 1.02 / 1.00 (comparable).
- The window at l.181 is identical for both readings, so l.184 alone decides. 10 <= 14.1 gives RECOVERED; 10 <= 6.3 (or the 9.0 used in calibration) fails, giving AMBIGUOUS.

The doc's l.87 relies on 'whose σ is 2.1 min'.
findings.fix:
Before publication:
- Add a dated erratum for PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:35 stating that the v2 CSV's σ 2.1 min is the value of record and 4.7 is the superseded v1 value.
- In CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE, state which σ source (the hashed CSV) sets both gates.
- Add this item to the hierarchy statement already required by the upheld product/reference-value blocker.

findings.title: The procedure document's 'Observed timing' claim (real transits +10 to +18 min off the frozen ephemeris) is contradicted for S96 by the authors' own registration and by an independent fit. It presents estimator scatter as an ephemeris error.
findings.location: results/CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md:87; results/vet_allsky/120444365/PREREGISTRATION_v2.md:7; scripts/prereg_conformance.py:181-184 (offset from max-SNR over band durations)
findings.evidence:
**What the document claims (l.87):** 'TIC 120444365's real transits sit +10 to +18 min from its frozen v2 ephemeris, whose σ is 2.1 min'. The +10 is S105 and the +18 is S96 (conf_real, joint offsets 10.0 and 18.0; the locked 2.0-h band fit gives +16).

**What the registration says (PREREGISTRATION_v2.md:7, QLP SAP):** S96 O-C +0.2 ± 1.8 min; S105 +8.0 ± 5.4; S69 -7.4 ± 4.2.
- S105 is consistent with the document.
- S96 differs from the evaluator's value by about 9 sigma.

**Independent fixed-shape fit** (wf_review/completeness/timing/indep.py and indep.out). Same QUALITY, mask and wotan settings as the evaluator; trapezoid with ingress 4 min; common offset; white-noise Δχ².
- S96 at 2.18 h (shape-implied): 0.0 [-1.5, +1.5] min, matching the registration. +16 min is disfavoured by Δχ² = 13.7 (about 10 after a β² ~1.3 red-noise allowance).
- S96 at the locked 2.0 h: bimodal, best +40.5, with 0 still inside Δχ² = 1.15. So the S96 mid-time depends on the estimator and on duration. It is not established as an ephemeris offset (nor does this prove the ephemeris exact).
- S69 at 2.18 h: -7.5 min, matching the registration. The evaluator gave -32 (QLP) / -30 (TESS-SPOC) on S69 (prod/s69_*.json).
- Caveat: my coverage test lacks the baseline requirement, so S96 used 5 events against the evaluator's 4.

**Authors' calibration, correctly timed injections** (conf_calib_[0-9] + conf_calib2_[0-9]). The evaluator is unbiased but noisy:
- S96: median 0.0, rms 8.3 min, 28% beyond 6.3 min.
- S105: median 0.0, rms 11.9, 33% beyond 6.3.

The real S96 +18 therefore sits at about 2 sigma of the estimator's own scatter. The min() gate (6.3 min) is below the estimator's timing resolution, so a min() failure measures the estimator, not the ephemeris. The document does not say this.
findings.fix:
Rewrite l.87:
- Report the S96/S105 offsets as conformance-estimator values.
- Quote the registration's per-sector O-C next to them.
- State the estimator's own timing scatter from the injections (rms 8-12 min for 120444365) and that it exceeds the 6.3-min min() gate.
- Optionally report a fixed-duration (T14_ref) timing alongside the max-SNR offset in each output JSON.

findings.title: The product of record is not enforced. The same 'QLP SAP_FLUX' config accepts a TESS-SPOC file, which changes the in-sample outcome. No rule says which product or release counts.
findings.location: scripts/prereg_conformance.py:52-59,113-117 (only SECTOR, TICID and column name are checked; ORIGIN is not), :111 (output records only lc path and sha); configs/conformance/*.json ('product': 'QLP' is used only for the clock gate at :123); prereg_protocol/PREREG_PROTOCOL.tex:39 ('first public light curve of the test sector'); results/CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE_2026-10-20.md:40
findings.evidence:
**Setup.** One config (wf_review/completeness/prod/s69_cfg.json): TIC 120444365, sector 69, product QLP, SAP_FLUX, locked 855 ppm / 2.0 h, σ 2.1, back-projected from final_ephemeris_v2.json. Run on two files:
- data/qlp_allsky/hlsp_qlp_tess_ffi_s0069-0000000120444365_tess_v01_llc.fits (ORIGIN MIT/QLP).
- data/lk_cache/.../hlsp_tess-spoc_tess_phot_0000000120444365-s0069_tess_v1_lc.fits (ORIGIN NASA/Ames, PROCVER spoc-5.0.103-20231116).

Both were accepted without warning, and the eligible events and outcome differ:

| File | Outcome | Eligible | Point scatter | Band fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QLP | AMBIGUOUS | 3/5 | 1761 ppm | -32 min, 2.6 h, SNR 4.27 |
| TESS-SPOC | RECOVERED | 4/5 | 1407 ppm | -30 min (exactly at the 30-min gate), 2.4 h, 878 ppm, SNR 6.78 |

The output JSONs record only 'lc' and 'lc_sha256'; no ORIGIN, PROCVER, DATA_REL or release version.

**Why this is a live risk:**
- The protocol's rule is 'first public light curve' (tex:39).
- TESS-SPOC FFI products exist for this target (S2/S29/S69 on disk).
- Only 183374279's amendment commits to waiting for QLP. The other six configs have no such rule.
- A grep for v01|reprocess|re-releas|first public|ORIGIN|TESS-SPOC|tglc in the doc, configs, evaluator and clarification finds no rule on which QLP release counts if S106 is reprocessed (for example after the S99-S105 timing fix).

**Prior coverage.** skeptic_clock_record/foreign* already showed that clock records are applied without cross-checking their qlp_sha256, TIC or sector. skeptic_depthgate ran SPOC files for another purpose. The ORIGIN/product half of this finding is new.
findings.fix:
Before any S106 photometry is examined:
- Make the evaluator refuse a file whose header ORIGIN and filename pattern do not match the config's product (MIT/QLP, hlsp_qlp_*_llc.fits).
- Record ORIGIN, PROCVER/DATA_REL, filename and header DATE in the output.
- Declare in the procedure which release counts (for example the first QLP release of the sector, all later re-releases reported but not scored).
- Extend the 183374279 'wait for QLP' rule to all seven configs.

findings.title: The software environment is not pinned: the requirements file in all three Zenodo bundles is empty, and outputs record no library versions.
findings.evidence:
- requirements_venv.txt is 0 bytes (sha e3b0c44298fc..., the empty-string hash) in all three bundle zips and in prereg_bundle/.
- git ls-tree -r HEAD in public_release has no requirements, environment or lock file.
- The procedure doc pins script SHA-256s only.
- The evaluator's output JSON has no package versions.
- Installed stack: numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1, wotan 2.0, astropy 8.0.2, pandas 2.3.3, numba 0.68.0.
- The outcome depends on wotan's biweight (l.132), scipy's chi2.sf (l.163) and numpy's median/MAD.
- I did not test whether a different version changes any outcome.
findings.fix: Publish a pinned lock file (the output of pip freeze from .venv) with the conformance release. Record its hash in CONFORMANCE_PROCEDURE, and write the key package versions into every output JSON.

findings.title: Real-data validation injects signals in raw QLP time, but the evaluator then shifts times by the clock correction. S105 injections therefore sit +1.6 to +4.4 min late by construction.
findings.location: scripts/validate_conformance_real.py:28 (ff[|t - tc| < dur/48] on raw t); scripts/prereg_conformance.py:127-128 (t = t + corr)
findings.evidence:
- The injection mask is computed on the raw FITS TIME.
- For sectors >= 99 the evaluator adds np.interp(t, event_btjd, correction_min).
- The conf_real S105 clock records give corrections of 1.6-4.4 min (for example 183374279: 2.01 / 3.27 / 4.42 min; 120444365: 1.64-3.7 min).
- So each injected box sits at tc + corr in the frame where it is scored.
- The bias is not visible above the scatter: the 120444365 S105 injections have median offset 0.0 and mean -2.8 min.
- It only affects the min()-reading power figure (the doc's '31/51 (61%)', computed with a 9-min calibration gate), not the max() rates.
findings.fix: Inject at tc - corr(tc) in raw time, using the same clock record, so that the injected signal is exactly at the prediction after correction. Re-quote the min()-reading power.
